item.title: Intensity-controlled Raster Scanning Carbon Ion Radiation Therapy With a Heavy-ion Gantry: Clinical Experience at Heidelberg Ion Beam Therapy Center.
item.dc:creator: Dvornikovich K, Held T, Franke H, Cakir C, Dörsam L, Manzey T, Jiang ZC, Winter S, Sittinger M, Winter M, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Dvornikovich K, Held T, Franke H, Cakir C, Dörsam L, Manzey T, Jiang ZC, Winter S, Sittinger M, Winter M, et al.
Journal: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics | DOI: 10.1016/j.ijrobp.2026.09.003
Published: 2026-Dec-01
PMID: 43044650



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Carbon ions have biophysical advantages over photons, including a finite range, increased relative biological effectiveness, and lowered oxygen dependence. Maximum treatment flexibility is attainable with rotational beam delivery. We report our clinical experience using the carbon-ion gantry at the Heidelberg Ion Beam Therapy Center with intensity-controlled raster scanning capability, focusing on treatment toxicity. METHODS AND MATERIALS: A total of 1622 patients treated using the carbon-ion gantry between 2012 and 2026 were evaluated. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Toxicity analysis was conducted using Common Terminology Criteria of Adverse Events v5.0. RESULTS: The median age preradiation therapy was 59 years (range, 18-91). Most patients had locally advanced tumors (21.8% T4; 11.2% T3) without regional lymph node metastases (45.4% N0). The most common treatment indications were sacrococcygeal tumors (n = 331; 20.4%), followed by tumors of the paranasal sinuses (n = 166; 10.2%) and the spine (n = 121; 7.5%). A total of 486 patients (30.0%) received carbon-ion reirradiation, the most frequent carbon-ion gantry treatment indication viewed across all patients. The most common particle therapy beam-angle number was 2 (range, 1-7). The use of more than 2 beam angles was particularly frequent in tumors of the skull base (45.8%) and the thoracic region (40.0%). High-grade (III and IV) acute and late toxicity rates were 2.4% and 4.2% in primary treatment. Mean numbers of acute and late grade I and II toxicity events per patient were 2.2 (95% confidence interval, 2.0-2.4) and 2.0 (95% confidence interval, 1.7-2.4), respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Carbon-ion radiation therapy using a heavy-ion gantry resulted in favorable toxicity rates in specific indications. Further interdisciplinary research demonstrating the clinical benefit of carbon-ion radiation therapy is required. This study provides more evidence supporting particle therapy facilities and may serve as a foundation for prospective clinical trials.

item.title: Clinical-pathological nodal discordance and survival outcomes in oral squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Chang CW, Liao LJ, Hung CY, Cheng PC, Cheng YP, Chiang CJ, Lee WC, Hsu WL, Chen TC
item.description:
Authors: Chang CW, Liao LJ, Hung CY, Cheng PC, Cheng YP, Chiang CJ, Lee WC, Hsu WL, Chen TC
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108233
Published: 2026-Nov-20
PMID: 43063685



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic significance of discordance between clinical and pathological nodal staging in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) remains poorly understood. This study investigates how clinical-pathological nodal discordance impacts survival outcomes in OSCC. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 14,618 OSCC patients from the Taiwan Cancer Registry who underwent primary surgical resection with neck dissection between 2018 and 2022. Patients were stratified into four groups: true negative (cN0pN0), occult metastasis (cN0pN + ), overt metastasis (cN + pN + ), and false positive (cN + pN0). Survival outcomes were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis, propensity score matching, and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression. RESULTS: Among 14,618 patients, 7,154 (48.9 %) were true negative, 1,290 (8.8 %) had occult metastasis, 3,197 (21.9 %) had overt metastasis, and 2,977 (20.4 %) were false positive. Approximately 30 % of patients presented with clinical-pathological discordance in neck staging. Despite harboring more advanced T-stage primary tumors, false-positive patients achieved survival outcomes comparable to those of true-negative patients (5-year DFS 71.6 % vs. 71.3 %; OS 76.1 % vs. 75.8 %). Extranodal extension (ENE) was present in 25.5 % of occult metastasis patients and 53.2 % of overt metastasis patients. Regardless of occult or overt presentation, the presence of ENE dictated similarly poor survival outcomes compared with patients without ENE (p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: Clinical-pathological nodal discordance is common in OSCC, and ENE, rather than the clinical detectability of nodal disease, is the dominant prognostic factor in node-positive disease. Elective neck dissection therefore serves a dual diagnostic and therapeutic role, identifying occult metastases that elude preoperative imaging and improving long-term survival.

item.title: Cancer risk with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists: An umbrella review of meta-analyses.
item.dc:creator: Petrelli F, Meregalli G, Berzi D, Nicolì F, Viglino F, Della Pepa G, Indovina F, Dalmiglio C, Forloni F, Bossi A, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Petrelli F, Meregalli G, Berzi D, Nicolì F, Viglino F, Della Pepa G, Indovina F, Dalmiglio C, Forloni F, Bossi A, et al.
Journal: Cancer epidemiology | DOI: 10.1016/j.canep.2026.103273
Published: 2026-Nov-20
PMID: 43063527



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Use of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) for diabetes and obesity is increasing, but effects on uncommon or long-latency cancers are uncertain. We synthesised meta-analytic evidence for overall and site-specific cancer risk and assessed methodological quality, overlap, outcome-level certainty, and credibility. METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from inception to 30 June 2026 for meta-analyses of GLP-1RAs or the dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist tirzepatide and incident cancer. Randomised and observational evidence was considered separately; review-level estimates were not recombined. We assessed methodological confidence with AMSTAR 2, overlap with corrected covered area (CCA), outcome-level certainty with a GRADE-informed algorithm, and association credibility with Ioannidis criteria. FINDINGS: We included 38 meta-analyses from 2012 to 2026. The most comprehensive placebo-controlled randomised evidence (48 trials, 94 245 participants, median follow-up 70 weeks) showed no statistically significant association with thyroid cancer (odds ratio [OR] 1·37, 95% CI 0·82-2·31; 1 fewer to 9 more cases per 10 000 treated), pancreatic cancer (0·84, 0·53-1·35), colorectal cancer (1·11, 0·75-1·65), or breast cancer (0·95, 0·60-1·49), and no overall cancer increase (OR 1·05, 0·98-1·13 across 50 trials). Thyroid and agent-specific haematological signals were inconsistent or based on sparse events; between-review discordance for thyroid and colorectal cancer was largely attributable to comparator restriction, choice of estimator, and handling of zero-event trials rather than to differences in cancer ascertainment. Observational syntheses suggested lower hepatocellular carcinoma risk (hazard ratio 0·60, 95% CI 0·41-0·88), but four reviews had very high overlap (CCA 50·0%). Outcome-level certainty was moderate for five outcomes, low for 11, and very low for five; none was high. No association met class I or II credibility criteria. INTERPRETATION: Randomised evidence shows no evidence of a material increase in overall or site-specific cancer risk over currently observed trial durations (median about 70 weeks, maximum about 5 years), and cancer concerns alone do not justify withholding indicated GLP-1RA treatment. Small, rare, long-latency, dose-specific, or agent-specific effects cannot be excluded, and the evidence cannot address exposure beyond approximately five years, well short of the 8-10 years generally required to evaluate cancer incidence. Observational protective associations should not support causal or cancer-prevention claims. FUNDING: None.

item.title: Effects of proton pump inhibitors on serum and fecal biomarkers and intestinal microbiota in dogs.
item.dc:creator: Romano FS, Barbosa IS, Melchert A, Amaral AR, Vendramini THA, Suchodolski J, Lallo MA
item.description:
Authors: Romano FS, Barbosa IS, Melchert A, Amaral AR, Vendramini THA, Suchodolski J, Lallo MA
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0361194
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43063192



Abstract:
The gastrointestinal tract of mammals, including dogs and cats, is inhabited by a highly diverse intestinal microbiota that plays an essential role in both health and disease. This microbial ecosystem influences various processes such as metabolism, immunity, neurodevelopment, and the maintenance of homeostasis and can be altered in many circumstances such as diseases, the use of oral medications and gastrointestinal pH. Proton Pump Inhibitors are suspected of causing dysbiosis due to the alteration of gastric pH. This study evaluated the effects PPIs on the microbiota of healthy dogs. Twenty Golden Retrievers were randomly allocated into four treatment groups (n = 5 per group): Omeprazole (OMP - 1 mg/kg twice a day), Esomeprazole (ESO - 1 mg/kg twice a day), Lansoprazole (LSP - 0.5 mg/kg twice a day), and Control (Placebo, CTL) and treated for 30 days. Feces were collected at the beginning (T0) and end (T30) of the trial for evaluation of dysbiosis index and blood biochemistry was performed to quantify target variables of gastrointestinal diseases (folate, cobalamin, iron and calcium) at the same period. Gastrin serum concentrations were evaluated at T0 and T30 only for the LSP group. Results showed no clinical signs or changes in the global dysbiosis index among treatments. However, specific microbial alterations were observed, including a reduction in Turicibacter in the OMP and ESO groups, and an increase in Streptococcus spp. in few individuals in the OMP group. Serum biomarkers related to inflammation and gastrointestinal absorption remained unchanged. In this study, PPIs did not induce intestinal dysbiosis or caused any clinical impairment, although some isolated microbial changes were noted.

item.title: Influence of peri-implant soft tissue thickness on marginal bone loss following immediate implant placement in the anterior maxilla: A retrospective comparative study.
item.dc:creator: Kadkhodazadeh M, Alam M, Golkar M, Naghshbandi T
item.description:
Authors: Kadkhodazadeh M, Alam M, Golkar M, Naghshbandi T
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0360723
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43063175



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Marginal bone stability is a critical determinant of the long-term success and esthetic harmony of dental implants. Peri-implant soft tissue thickness (STT) has been proposed as a biological factor influencing crestal bone remodeling. This retrospective comparative study aimed to evaluate the relationship between peri-implant STT and marginal bone loss (MBL) following immediate implant placement in the anterior maxilla after one year of functional loading. METHODS: Fifty immediate implant sites from 50 patients were retrospectively analyzed. Based on mid-buccal soft tissue measurement, implants were classified as thin (STT ≤ 1 mm; n = 22) or thick (STT > 1 mm; n = 28) phenotypes. Clinical parameters, including probing depth, bleeding on probing, plaque index, keratinized tissue width, and pink esthetic score, and radiographic parameters (MBL) were extracted from patient records. MBL was measured on standardized periapical digital radiographs taken immediately after surgery and at one-year follow-up using a custom positioning index. RESULTS: The mean age of participants was 57.88 ± 11.16 years. MBL was significantly higher in the thin soft tissue group (1.34 ± 0.19 mm) compared with the thick tissue group (1.00 ± 0.20 mm; p < 0.0001). STT exhibited a strong negative correlation with MBL (r = -0.749, p < 0.0001). Other variables showed no significant intergroup differences. No significant difference in MBL was observed between implant systems. CONCLUSION: Within the limitations of this retrospective study, peri-implant soft tissue thickness was identified as a key determinant of marginal bone preservation after immediate implant placement in the anterior maxilla. Thicker mucosa was associated with significantly reduced bone resorption and more stable peri-implant esthetic outcomes after one year.

item.title: Induction Immunochemotherapy Followed by Definitive Chemoradiotherapy and Consolidation Immunotherapy for Locally Advanced Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Prospective Phase II Study.
item.dc:creator: Lin L, Li H, Song X, Zhao L, Cheng Y, Liu M, Yu W, Zhang Q, Cai X, Yang Y, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Lin L, Li H, Song X, Zhao L, Cheng Y, Liu M, Yu W, Zhang Q, Cai X, Yang Y, et al.
Journal: International journal of cancer | DOI: 10.1002/ijc.70828
Published: 2026-Nov-19
PMID: 43059192



Abstract:
Long-term survival after definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy (dCCRT) remains limited in locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). We evaluated induction immunochemotherapy followed by dCCRT and consolidation immunotherapy in this setting. This prospective, single-arm Phase II study enrolled 54 adults selected for definitive nonsurgical treatment. The planned regimen comprised two cycles of induction immunochemotherapy with nab-paclitaxel, carboplatin, and a programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) inhibitor, followed by dCCRT with 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions and concurrent weekly chemotherapy. The same PD-1 inhibitor was planned as consolidation therapy for up to 1 year. The primary endpoint was the 2-year overall survival (OS) rate. Fifty-three patients (98.1%) completed two induction cycles, all 54 proceeded to dCCRT, and 31 (57.4%) received consolidation immunotherapy. Among all 54 enrolled patients, the 2-year OS and progression-free survival (PFS) rates were 84.6% (95% confidence interval [CI], 75.2%-95.0%) and 61.5% (95% CI, 49.5%-76.4%), respectively, after a median follow-up of 28.1 months. Adverse events occurred predominantly during dCCRT and were mainly hematologic; lymphopenia and esophagitis were among the most frequent toxicities. Exploratory analyses suggested that suboptimal response after induction immunochemotherapy was associated with shorter PFS. The survival outcomes observed with this sequential approach support further evaluation of its comparative clinical benefit in randomized studies. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05621707).

item.title: Rethinking Oncologic Trismus: Evidence for an Undermeasured Soft Tissue Phenotype.
item.dc:creator: McMillan H, Cardoso R, Xiao Q, Cuccaro P, Sedory A, Fuller C, Hutcheson K
item.description:
Authors: McMillan H, Cardoso R, Xiao Q, Cuccaro P, Sedory A, Fuller C, Hutcheson K
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70559
Published: 2026-Nov-19
PMID: 43059079



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Soft tissue impairment spanning the lymphedema-fibrosis continuum and trismus are highly prevalent head and neck cancer toxicities. While fibrosis is often implicated in trismus, no prior study has directly examined the association between clinician-graded head and neck lymphedema and fibrosis (HNL/F) and maximal interincisal opening (MIO). METHODS: HNL/F classifications and MIO were evaluated in 832 cancer survivors at a specialized Trismus Clinic (2020-2025). Spearman's correlation, ANOVA, univariate, and multivariate linear regression examined HNL/F-MIO relationships overall and by region (face, neck, and intraoral). RESULTS: In unadjusted and adjusted analyses, all clinician-graded HNL/F classifications in the face were significantly associated with reduced MIO. In all regions, fibrosis was associated with reduced MIO in unadjusted models; after covariate adjustment, fibrosis remained significant, except in the neck. CONCLUSION: These findings provide the first evidence linking regional and severity-based HNL/F classification with MIO and support HNL/F phenotyping in trismus assessment.

item.title: Standardization and pitfalls of iENE in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: Optimizing diagnostic accuracy, prognostic staging and treatment selection.
item.dc:creator: De Felice F, Goanta L, Marchi F, Succo G, Maroldi R, Sanguineti G
item.description:
Authors: De Felice F, Goanta L, Marchi F, Succo G, Maroldi R, Sanguineti G
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108237
Published: 2026-Nov-19
PMID: 43057067



Abstract:
Extranodal extension (ENE) represents the cornerstone of adverse nodal staging in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). While pathological ENE (pENE) is the historical benchmark, the clinical push toward non-surgical primary organ preservation and surgical de-escalation has forced reliance on imaging-derived ENE (iENE). However, applying iENE to clinical decision-making introduces significant methodological and clinical dilemmas. Inspired by recent insights from radiotherapy de-intensification trials in oncology, where "less is not simple" and non-superiority is frequently misconstrued as non-inferiority, this critical review evaluates the evolution of iENE. We critically analyze the transition from unstandardized radiological reporting - "the pre-consensus era" - to international consensus frameworks - "the standardized reporting era" -, dissect the trade-offs between sensitivity, specificity, and disease prevalence and evaluate the incorporation of iENE into the 9th Edition UICC/AJCC TNM staging system. Ultimately, we distinguish the utility of iENE across three distinct clinical objectives: identifying pathological ENE, predicting oncological outcomes for staging and selecting patients for surgery versus chemoradiotherapy.

item.title: Targeting the IGF-estrogen receptor signaling nexus in thyroid cancer: From molecular crosstalk to precision therapeutics.
item.dc:creator: Margoni A, Papavassiliou KA, Papavassiliou AG
item.description:
Authors: Margoni A, Papavassiliou KA, Papavassiliou AG
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108234
Published: 2026-Nov-19
PMID: 43057066



Abstract:
The potential convergence of insulin-like growth factor (IGF) and estrogen receptor alpha (ERα) signaling represents a compelling molecular hypothesis in thyroid cancer, linking growth factor and hormonal responsiveness to malignant progression and therapeutic resistance. IGF signaling through IGF-1 receptor (IGF-1R) and insulin receptor isoform A (IR-A) activates phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)-AKT-mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) and mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathways, promoting proliferation and survival. An experimentally established IGF-2/IR-A autocrine loop further contributes to tumor-cell proliferation and impaired differentiation. Concurrently, ERα fosters proliferative and invasive phenotypes through keratin 19 (KRT19), potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily Q member 3 (KCNQ3)-associated MAPK activation, and epigenetic regulation, whereas estrogen receptor beta (ERβ) may exert context-dependent antiproliferative effects. Although reciprocal ERα-IGF-1R interactions have been demonstrated in non-thyroid models, direct molecular crosstalk in thyroid cancer remains unconfirmed. These findings provide a rationale for investigating ERα antagonism or degradation, selective ERβ activation, and IGF axis inhibition as potential therapeutic strategies. This article proposes that functional interplay between IGF and ERα signaling may create distinct oncogenic dependencies beyond the individual contributions of either pathway. Establishing such cooperation and determining whether combined inhibition offers advantages over individual targeting are essential steps toward evaluating its potential for biomarker-guided therapeutic development in thyroid cancer.

item.title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists and Survival in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Hunter AE, Uralov D, Byrd MC, Cannon TY, Curry J, Osazuwa-Peters N
item.description:
Authors: Hunter AE, Uralov D, Byrd MC, Cannon TY, Curry J, Osazuwa-Peters N
Journal: JAMA otolaryngology-- head & neck surgery | DOI: 10.1001/jamaoto.2026.3648
Published: 2026-Nov-19
PMID: 43056129



Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Metformin has known metabolic effects and associated survival benefits in head and neck cancer. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) also modulate systemic metabolism through regulating blood glucose levels and lipid metabolism. OBJECTIVE: To investigate whether GLP-1RAs are associated with survival outcomes in patients with head and neck cancers. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective cohort study was conducted using clinical data from January 1, 1990, through December 1, 2025, from the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Adults with histologically confirmed head and neck squamous cell carcinomas (HNSCC) were included. Data were analyzed in January 2026. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was overall survival for all HNSCC and stratified by site. The secondary outcome was overall survival among patients concurrently using GLP-1RAs and metformin. Adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) with 95% CIs were estimated. RESULTS: There were 4532 patients (mean [SD] age, 63.4 [10.9] years; 1638 female individuals [36.1%] and 2891 male individuals [63.8%]) included in the cohort. Across all subsites, GLP-1RA users had significantly improved overall survival compared with controls at 1-year (aHR, 0.42; 95% CI, 0.36-0.49), 3-year (aHR, 0.48; 95% CI, 0.43-0.54), and 5-year intervals (aHR, 0.51; 95% CI, 0.46-0.57). By anatomic subsite, GLP-1RA use remained consistently associated with a lower hazard of mortality at 5-year intervals (oral cavity: aHR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.51-0.70; oropharynx: aHR, 0.51; 95% CI, 0.41-0.64; larynx: aHR, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.39-0.61). We also observed significant overall survival among patients who used GLP-1RAs and metformin at 1 year (aHR, 0.29; 95% CI, 0.23-0.36), 3 years (aHR, 0.36; 95% CI, 0.30-0.42) and 5 years (aHR, 0.39; 95% CI, 0.34-0.45). CONCLUSIONS: The findings of this cohort study suggest that there may be survival benefits associated with GLP-1RA use among patients with HNSCC across several subsites. Future prospective and interventional studies of GLP-1RA potential metabolic adjuncts in oncologic care may help corroborate the associations from this retrospective study.

item.title: Integrating genetic and lung tissue proteomics data to identify susceptibility proteins for lung cancer.
item.dc:creator: Xu S, Shi J, Shu XO, Tao R, Dou Y, Guo X, Wen W, Yang Y, Zhang B, Wu J, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Xu S, Shi J, Shu XO, Tao R, Dou Y, Guo X, Wen W, Yang Y, Zhang B, Wu J, et al.
Journal: Journal of the National Cancer Institute | DOI: 10.1093/jnci/djag424
Published: 2026-Nov-19
PMID: 43055353



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Proteins directly impact disease development and act as drug targets. We integrated genetic and lung tissue proteomic data to identify lung cancer susceptibility proteins and evaluated them as candidate drug targets. METHOD: We profiled the proteome and genome in 200 non-neoplastic lung tissue samples and constructed genetic models to predict protein abundance. These models were applied to genome-wide association study (GWAS) data of 55,174 lung cancer cases and 1,294,174 controls to evaluate associations between predicted abundance and lung cancer risk overall and by major histological subtypes. Independent lung tissue proteomic data was used for cross-dataset evaluation, followed by colocalization and summary-data-based Mendelian randomization. Prioritized proteins were cross-referenced against drug databases. RESULTS: We identified 29 lung cancer risk-associated proteins at a false discovery rate < 5%, including 25 for overall lung cancer, two (AQP3 and IL18) specific to adenocarcinoma, and two (HMGN2 and HLA-DMB) specific to squamous cell carcinoma. Genes encoding 15 proteins are located > 2Mb away from known GWAS risk loci. Among the remaining 14 proteins at known risk loci, five (EPHX2, CLDN18, PSMD5, ARHGAP27, and CYP2S1) showed associations independent of proximal lead variant. Of the 29 proteins, eight were predicted and six were significant in independent data. DSP, IL18 and TYMP proteins demonstrated both reproducible and potential causal evidence and are targeted by six drugs that are FDA-approved or in phase III trials. CONCLUSION: Our study identified novel lung cancer susceptibility proteins and potential therapeutic targets, offering insights into lung cancer biology and informing future translational research.

item.title: Local and distant site definitive treatment in metastatic oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma: A national cancer database analysis.
item.dc:creator: West JD, Lin ME, Ziltzer RS, Ulloa R, Kim I, Swanson MS
item.description:
Authors: West JD, Lin ME, Ziltzer RS, Ulloa R, Kim I, Swanson MS
Journal: American journal of otolaryngology | DOI: 10.1016/j.amjoto.2026.104986
Published: 2026-Nov-18
PMID: 43063590



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Assess effect of local and distant site definitive treatment on overall survival (OS) in patients receiving chemotherapy for metastatic oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (M1 OPSCC). METHODS: Adult M1 OPSCC patients treated with chemotherapy (2010-2017) were identified via the National Cancer Database. Primary outcomes were median and 3-year OS, stratified by HPV status. The primary predictor was additional definitive treatment target: local site (LST), distant site (DST), or both (LDST). Pairwise and Kaplan-Meier log-rank tests and multivariable Cox regression assessed the impact of treatment site on OS by HPV status. Multiple imputation addressed incomplete HPV data. RESULTS: Of 2684 patients, 70.3% had missing HPV status; five imputed datasets were generated. LST was the most common additional treatment (61.7%). Combined local and distant treatment (LDST) yielded the highest median survival overall (24.1 months) and in both HPV-positive (27.7 months) and HPV-negative (18.1 months) subgroups. Pairwise log-rank comparisons showed any additional definitive treatment improved 3-year OS regardless of HPV status. On multivariate regression controlling for clinical characteristics, LDST reduced 3-year mortality risk versus DST alone in both HPV-positive (HR = 0.60, 95% CI 0.50-0.70, p < 0.0001) and HPV-negative (HR = 0.66, 95% CI 0.58-0.75, p < 0.0001) disease. CONCLUSIONS: In this NCDB analysis, adding definitive treatment to chemotherapy in M1 OPSCC is associated with improved overall survival. Although our study is limited by selection bias and limited retrospective data in small sample sizes, our findings suggest that further prospective investigation should be considered to determine whether definitive treatment is warranted in select patients undergoing chemotherapy to improve locoregional control.

item.title: Megestrol Acetate for Prevention of Weight Loss During Modern Radiotherapy in Patients With Head and Neck Cancer: A Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.dc:creator: Muangwong P, Samakgarn V, Malasri P, Toapichattrakul P, Chitapanarux I
item.description:
Authors: Muangwong P, Samakgarn V, Malasri P, Toapichattrakul P, Chitapanarux I
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70558
Published: 2026-Nov-18
PMID: 43053594



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Weight loss is a common complication during radiotherapy for head and neck cancer and may adversely affect treatment tolerance and outcomes. We evaluated whether megestrol acetate (MA) prevents treatment-related weight loss. METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label randomized controlled trial, 102 patients with non-nasopharyngeal head and neck squamous cell carcinoma undergoing radiotherapy were assigned to MA plus standard care or standard care alone. Standard care consisted of nutritional counseling, symptom management, and feeding-tube placement when clinically indicated. The primary endpoint was change in body weight from baseline to 6 weeks post-radiotherapy. RESULTS: At 6 weeks post-radiotherapy, the MA group showed a mean weight gain of 2.07 kg, whereas the control group lost 1.74 kg (p < 0.01). Weight gain was primarily due to increased fat mass, with no significant difference in muscle mass. Quality of life was similar between groups. CONCLUSION: MA improved weight preservation during radiotherapy and may serve as an adjunct to supportive care in head and neck cancer. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: TCTR20240330005.

item.title: Variation in Basal Serum Cortisol Levels During Treatment of Oral Lichen Planus With 0.5% Triamcinolone Acetonide Mouthrinses: A Prospective Observational Study.
item.dc:creator: Blanco-Aguilera E, Gándara-Vila P, Sanmartín-Barragáns V, Rodríguez-García J, Marichalar-Mendía X, Blanco-Aguilera A, Lorenzo-Pouso AI, Otero-Rey E, Blanco-Carrión A
item.description:
Authors: Blanco-Aguilera E, Gándara-Vila P, Sanmartín-Barragáns V, Rodríguez-García J, Marichalar-Mendía X, Blanco-Aguilera A, Lorenzo-Pouso AI, Otero-Rey E, Blanco-Carrión A
Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70568
Published: 2026-Nov-18
PMID: 43053526



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate changes in basal serum cortisol levels in patients with atrophic-erosive oral lichen planus (OLP) and oral lichenoid lesion (OLL) treated with 0.5% triamcinolone acetonide mouthrinses and to assess the occurrence of clinical manifestations associated with adrenal dysfunction. METHODS: A prospective observational study was conducted in 68 patients with clinically and histopathologically confirmed atrophic-erosive OLP or OLL. Participants received 0.5% triamcinolone acetonide mouthrinses following a tapering regimen over 3 months. Basal serum cortisol levels were measured at baseline, after 30 days, and after 90 days of treatment. Clinical and demographic variables and treatment-related adverse effects were analyzed. RESULTS: Mean basal serum cortisol levels decreased from 17.05 ± 4.38 μg/dL at baseline to 8.79 ± 7.34 μg/dL after 1 month of treatment. Following dose tapering, serum cortisol levels (SCL) partially recovered to 11.94 ± 6.44 μg/dL at 3 months. No clinical manifestations of adrenal insufficiency were observed. Baseline SCL were significantly associated with serum cortisol concentrations after 1 month (r = 0.34; p < 0.05). Older patients exhibited smaller hormonal fluctuations during treatment. CONCLUSIONS: Triamcinolone acetonide induced a transient reduction in SCL without clinically relevant adrenal dysfunction, suggesting a limited systemic impact when administered a tapering regimen.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to adapt the Oral Health-Related Quality of Life for Adolescents with Down Syndrome (OH-QOLADS) scale into Turkish and evaluate its psychometric properties. It also explored oral health status and quality of life among children with Down syndrome (DS). METHODS: The study included 100 children with DS and their mothers. Sociodemographic and oral health data were collected through structured questionnaires. The OH-QOLADS, comprising child and family forms with two timeframes, was translated and culturally adapted following international guidelines. Internal consistency, CFA, and item-total correlations were conducted to assess psychometric validity. RESULTS: The Turkish OH-QOLADS showed excellent internal consistency (Cronbach's α and McDonald's ω > 0.94) across all forms and timeframes. Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis of worldwide prevalence of geographic tongue (GT) in healthy children and adolescents. Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Approximately 20% of patients with oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) develop distant metastases (DM). Survival outcomes after DM vary widely depending on clinical and biologic factors. This study compared baseline characteristics, management strategies, and oncologic outcomes among OPSCC patients with primary and secondary DM to better inform prognostication and therapeutic planning. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients treated at a tertiary care center with HPV/p16-positive, HPV/p16-negative, or unknown-status OPSCC who developed DM at any point. Treatments included surgery, radiation, and systemic therapy delivered with curative or non-curative intent. Cohort characteristics and overall survival (OS), stratified by primary versus secondary DM and treatment subgroups, were assessed using chi-square tests and Kaplan Meier analyses. RESULTS: A total of 132 patients were included: 18 with primary DM and 114 with secondary DM. HPV-positivity was lower in primary versus secondary DM group (22.2% vs 75.4%). Median follow-up was 32.4 months. Median OS from DM diagnosis was significantly shorter for primary versus secondary DM (9.6 vs 20.4 months; HR 2.00, 95% CI 1.16-3.46). CONCLUSIONS: This is the largest single center analysis of DM OPSCC to date. Primary DM OPSCC was associated with worse survival and lower HPV-positivity. Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Depth of invasion, perineural invasion, lymphovascular invasion, and worst pattern of invasion (WPOI) increasingly guide management of early-stage oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OCSCC), yet their prognostic value across clinically relevant outcomes remains incompletely synthesized. We systematically reviewed and meta-analyzed their association with nodal metastasis, recurrence, and survival. METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and trial registries were searched for cohort studies of these predictors in surgically treated early-stage OCSCC (T1-T2N0M0). Study quality was assessed and data extracted per PRISMA 2020. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed when outcomes were compatible, with sensitivity analyses restricted to multivariable estimates and to alternative harmonization choices. Certainty of evidence was graded using GRADE. RESULTS: Forty studies (15 674 patients) met inclusion criteria; 30 were meta-analyzed. Perineural invasion was associated with worse disease-free survival (HR: 2.23, 95% CI: 1.80-2.77), recurrence, and nodal metastasis (OR: 4.06, 95% CI: 2.22-7.42). CONCLUSIONS: Perineural invasion, depth of invasion, lymphovascular invasion, and WPOI were each associated with adverse outcomes in early-stage OCSCC, particularly nodal metastasis. These estimates derive from heterogeneous retrospective studies and do not allow ranking of the predictors against one another. Prospective studies with standardized definitions and adjusted analyses are needed.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether intrapartum hyoscine butylbromide, sodium bicarbonate, and their combination increase the rate of spontaneous vaginal birth in nulliparous women undergoing induction of labour. DESIGN: Multicentre, randomised, double blind, placebo controlled, 2×2 factorial phase 3 trial (SAINT). SETTING: 11 Norwegian hospitals providing comprehensive obstetric care. PARTICIPANTS: Nulliparous women aged 18-50 years with a singleton live fetus in cephalic presentation at term with an indication for induction of labour. INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) to oral sodium bicarbonate (4×1 g per dose) plus intravenous hyoscine butylbromide (20 mg per dose), oral sodium bicarbonate plus intravenous placebo, oral placebo plus intravenous hyoscine butylbromide, or double placebo. The investigational medicinal product was administered at the onset of active labour and repeated every four hours to a maximum of three doses. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE: Spontaneous vaginal birth (no instrumental or caesarean delivery). RESULTS: Between 4 January 2023 and 29 January 2025, 3094 nulliparous women were randomised, and 2963 comprised the full analysis set. Spontaneous vaginal birth occurred in 57% (422/741) in the bicarbonate plus hyoscine butylbromide arm, 61% (445/734) in the bicarbonate arm, 61% (449/741) in the hyoscine butylbromide arm, and 56% (422/747) in the double placebo arm. Marginal risk differences for spontaneous vaginal birth compared with double placebo were -0.2 (95% confidence interval -5.1 to 4.7; P=0.93) percentage points for combined treatment, 3.1 (-1.7 to 8.0; P=0.21) percentage points for bicarbonate, and 4.0 (-0.8 to 8.9; P=0.10) percentage points for hyoscine butylbromide. Serious adverse events were similar between groups, and no treatment related serious morbidity or deaths were observed. CONCLUSIONS: No clear evidence was found that intrapartum hyoscine butylbromide, sodium bicarbonate, or their combination increased spontaneous vaginal birth compared with placebo. Abstract:
PURPOSE: To report a single arm multi-site phase II study evaluating a reduced contralateral neck elective nodal clinical target volume (enCTV) in p16+ oropharyngeal cancer (p16+OPC). METHODS AND MATERIALS: Newly diagnosed p16+OPC without contralateral nodal involvement but with clinical or pathological features warranting contralateral elective nodal treatment were eligible. Treatment included proton- or photon-based definitive (chemo)radiation or adjuvant (chemo)radiation following Transoral Robotic Surgery. All patients received SAVER enCTV and the primary endpoint was two-year elective out-of-field contralateral nodal failure. Dosimetric comparison between SAVER enCTV and consensus enCTV of the first 10 definitive and adjuvant patients was performed. Overall survival (OS), progression-free-survival (PFS), toxicities, and patient reported outcomes were analyzed. RESULTS: Fifty-two patients were enrolled, of which 36 (69.2%) received definitive (chemo)radiation. Thirty-five (67.3%) had bulky or multiple ipsilateral lymph nodes and 18 (34.6%) had significant smoking history. With median follow-up of 31.0 months (range 13 - 49 months), there were no contralateral nodal failures with an upper limit one-sided 95% confidence interval for contralateral nodal failure of 2.7%. Two-year OS and PFS were 92.2% (95% CI [88.5 - 95.9%]) and 86.2% (95% CI [81.4 - 91.0%]), respectively. Acute grade 3 toxicity was observed in 13 (25%) patients including 8 (15.4%) who received a gastrostomy tube. There were no grade 4-5 toxicities. CONCLUSION: Selective avoidance of nodal volumes at minimal risk in the N0 contralateral neck can be safely performed while maintaining excellent regional control in the definitive and adjuvant settings. item.title: Intrapartum oral azithromycin versus placebo alone or in combination with other antimicrobials on maternal infection in South East Asia.
item.dc:creator: Patel AB, Kurhe K, Bhargav S, Khedikar V, Waikar M, Shivkumar P, Goudar SS, Metgud MC, Kavi A, Derman R, et al.
item.description:

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In low-resource facilities that routinely use intrapartum prophylactic antimicrobials, the use of multiple antimicrobials could be rationalised by a single oral dose of oral azithromycin. METHODS: The Azithromycin Prevention in Labor Use Study (A-PLUS), a randomized double-blind, placebo-controlled trial performed across eight sites in seven countries amongst women who planned to deliver vaginally. They were randomly assigned to receive study drug, a single intrapartum 2 gm oral dose of azithromycin or an identical appearing placebo. Data from four South-East Asia sites (Indian sites Nagpur and Belagavi, Pakistan, and Bangladesh) was analyzed to evaluate whether the use of non-study antimicrobials (alone or in-combination) given after randomization through one-day postpartum for any indication (prophylactic or treatment) modified the effect of study drugs on maternal outcomes (maternal infections, antibiotic usage 2-42days postpartum on ambulatory basis or re-hospitalization). The non-study antimicrobials given after randomization through 1-day postpartum was defined by four exposure sub-groups within azithromycin and placebo arm as, Use of: i) No non-study antibiotic; ii) Cephalosporin only; iii) Other non-study non-cephalosporin antibiotics; and iv) Cephalosporin and other non-study non-cephalosporin antibiotics. An intent to treat (ITT) analysis was adopted. Adjusted relative risks and 95% confidence intervals comparing azithromycin with placebo were estimated using Poisson regression models with robust variance estimators that included study site, maternal non-study antimicrobial use, and a treatment-by-non-study antimicrobial use interaction term. RESULTS: All maternal non-study antibiotic subgroups had balanced randomization between azithromycin and placebo. The risk of any maternal infections was reduced when only azithromycin was received versus placebo (RR = 0.75; 95% CI-0.57-0.98) and when group iv antimicrobials were used with azithromycin compared to only group iv antimicrobials (RR = 0.79; 95% CI-0.66-0.95). The use of antibiotics from day2-42 was similar in both arms (azithromycin or placebo) with or without use of other antimicrobials. CONCLUSIONS: This secondary analysis found no evidence that non-study antimicrobials use modified the effect of azithromycin on maternal outcomes. This study underscores the importance of considering an easily administrable intrapartum prophylaxis of oral monotherapy in low resource, high risk for infections sites to reduce antimicrobial resistance due to multiple antimicrobial use.

Abstract:
Vernolac is a commercially available polyherbal formulation comprising Vernonia zeylanica aerial parts, Nigella sativa seeds, Hemidesmus indicus roots, Smilax glabra rhizome, and Leucas zeylanica aerial parts. Although previous in vitro studies have demonstrated the anticancer potential of Vernolac and its active ingredients, safety data are available only for some of the plant ingredients of Vernolac. In the present study, acute and 28-day repeat-dose toxicity of Vernolac were evaluated in Wistar rats in accordance with OECD guidelines 420 and 407, respectively. Acute toxicity was investigated for 14 days after administering a single oral dose of 2000 mg/kg to 10 animals (5 males, 5 females). A repeat-dose toxicity study was conducted, in which the human equivalent therapeutic dose in rats (HED; 165 mg/kg/day), a mid-dose (2 × HED; 330 mg/kg/day), and a high dose (4 × HED; 660 mg/kg/day) were administered to three separate groups, each comprising 10 naive animals (5 males and 5 females), for a period of 28 days. In both acute and repeat-dose studies, no morbidity, mortality, changes in food and water intake, relative organ weights, microscopic changes in organs, hematological changes, or clinical signs of toxicity were observed. In the acute study, a significant increase in AST and ALT levels was observed in males. In the 28-day repeated dose study, a significant reduction in ALT was observed only in females receiving 4x HED. In summary, the LD50 of Vernolac is above 2000 mg/kg, and a dose up to two times the therapeutic daily dose is non-toxic in Wistar rats over 28 days. The liver may be a target organ of toxicity when overdosed.

Abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to evaluate the knowledge, attitudes, and reported practices of mothers living in Jordan regarding childhood acute gastroenteritis and to identify factors associated with poor knowledge, poor practice, lack of oral rehydration solution (ORS) awareness, and antibiotic use without medical consultation. METHODS: An analytical cross-sectional study was conducted among 730 mothers living in Jordan using a structured Arabic-language questionnaire. Participants were recruited through paediatric hospital settings and social media using convenience sampling. Composite knowledge and practice scores were calculated, and four multivariable binary logistic-regression models were fitted to examine factors associated with the prespecified outcomes. RESULTS: The mean composite knowledge score was 15.73 ± 6.83 out of 28, corresponding to 56.18% of the maximum score, and 31.37% of participants were categorized as having poor knowledge. The mean composite practice score was 4.58 ± 1.71 out of 10, corresponding to 45.84% of the maximum score, and 61.23% were categorized as having poor practice. Overall, 54.52% identified three or fewer of the eight dehydration signs assessed, 59.59% were aware of ORS, and 3.15% selected ORS as their intended first action. Compared with residence in Central Jordan, residence in North Jordan was associated with higher adjusted odds of poor knowledge (aOR 2.18, 95% CI 1.38-3.45), poor practice (aOR 1.74, 95% CI 1.19-2.55), lack of ORS awareness (aOR 1.52, 95% CI 1.01-2.28), and antibiotic use without medical consultation (aOR 1.81, 95% CI 1.12-2.91). CONCLUSION: Important gaps were identified in dehydration-sign recognition, ORS-related intended practices, and overall reported home-management practices. These findings support the development and evaluation of targeted caregiver-education initiatives emphasizing dehydration recognition, appropriate ORS use, safe medication practices, and timely care-seeking. Regional and educational differences may help identify groups requiring additional support; however, the observed associations should not be interpreted causally because of the cross-sectional design.

item.title: Behavioural sleep quality and quantity and their associations with age, salivary cortisol and abnormal behaviours: A preliminary field study in racing thoroughbreds.
item.dc:creator: Hennes N, Greening L, McBride S, Lemarchand J, Cognié J, Foury A, Phelipon R, Bourguignon H, Ruet A, Lansade L
item.description:
Authors: Hennes N, Greening L, McBride S, Lemarchand J, Cognié J, Foury A, Phelipon R, Bourguignon H, Ruet A, Lansade L
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0342874
Published: 2026-01-01

Abstract:
Sleep plays a key role in both physical recovery and welfare. However, sleep patterns remain poorly documented in animals, particularly in athletic horses. This study aimed to provide a detailed description of sleep quantity and quality in training Thoroughbred racehorses and to investigate their relationships with age, abnormal behaviours, and cortisol. Thirteen Thoroughbreds (2-7 years old) were continuously monitored in their home environment for 48 hours. An ethogram was used to quantify sleep-related behaviours associated with the two main behavioural sleep states: non-rapid eye movement (NREM-like) and rapid eye movement (REM-like), as well as sleep interruptions (from day 1 at 12:00 to day 3 at 12:00). Sleep Quality Indices (SQIs), reflecting the relationship between sleep duration and sleep interruptions (SIs), were then calculated. Behavioural observations of four indicators of poor welfare (alertness, stereotypies, inactivity, aggressiveness towards humans) were performed using scan sampling, and salivary cortisol was measured each morning. Linear mixed-effects models were used to assess the links between sleep quantity and quality, age, mean cortisol, and abnormal behaviours. Age was significantly associated with behavioural sleep quantity, being positively associated with total behavioural NREM-related sleep (Wald test: χ2 = 5.40, p = 0.02), and negatively associated with total behavioural REM-related sleep (Wald test: χ2 = 4.36, p = 0.04) and total recumbency duration (Wald test: χ2 = 5.68, p = 0.02). Morning cortisol concentrations were negatively associated with Total SQI (Wald test: χ2 = 5.26, p = 0.02) and Combined SQI (Wald test: χ2 = 5.60, p = 0.02). Likewise, horses displaying abnormal behaviours more frequently had lower Total SQI (Wald test: χ2 = 4.07, p = 0.04), pointing to a potential link between stress or altered welfare and poorer sleep quality. These findings suggest that, whilst the type and duration of equine behavioural-related sleep may be mainly affected by age, sleep quality is associated with both cortisol levels and the expression of abnormal behaviours, indicating that poor sleep quality may be linked to poor welfare in this population of horses. Overall, these findings highlight behavioural sleep quality as a potential component of racehorse welfare assessment and warrant further investigation into the factors influencing sleep in athletic horses.

Abstract:
This multicenter case-control study assessed (2019-2023) the association of oral and anogenital human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes with head and neck cancers in Brazil. Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate preoperative risk stratification for lymph node metastasis (LNM) in papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) remains difficult. We developed and validated ThyLNT, a Transformer-based 2.5D deep learning model using preoperative computed tomography (CT), and explored related biological features in multi-omics analyses. METHODS: A total of 1560 patients with PTC from six hospitals were retrospectively included. The Tongji Hospital cohort was divided into training and internal validation sets, and five external cohorts were used for independent testing. Seven 2.5D tumor slices were extracted per patient, encoded with a DenseNet201 backbone, and fused by a Transformer. Model performance was compared with radiomics, ensemble learning, and multi-instance learning using AUC, calibration, decision curve, and precision-recall analyses. Bulk RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, and spatial metabolomics were used to explore related biological features. RESULTS: ThyLNT achieved an AUC of 0.882 (CI, 0.858-0.905) in the training cohort, 0.787 (CI, 0.738-0.835) in the internal validation cohort, and 0.772 (CI, 0.662-0.878) to 0.827 (CI, 0.763-0.885) across the five external cohorts. Multi-omics analyses provided exploratory biological context, including candidate associations with vascular endothelial growth factor A-related signaling and lipid metabolism. CONCLUSIONS: ThyLNT demonstrated multicenter performance for preoperative LNM prediction in PTC and may support risk stratification, although calibration, threshold use, and clinical utility require prospective validation.

Abstract:
PURPOSE: Mandibular advancement devices (MADs) are an established treatment for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), but reliable predictors of response remain limited. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study included 82 consecutive patients with OSA treated with MAD across six tertiary sleep centers. Baseline and follow-up home sleep apnea tests performed at least 6 months after completion of MAD titration were analyzed. POSA was defined according to Cartwright's criteria as a supine apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) at least twice the non-supine AHI. Outcomes included changes in respiratory parameters and treatment success according to Sher's criteria (≥50% AHI reduction and post-treatment AHI <20 events/h). RESULTS: Fifty patients had POSA and 32 had non-POSA. MAD therapy significantly improved total AHI, oxygen desaturation index, and oxygenation parameters in both groups. item.title: TM7x, an Ultrasmall Oral Episymbiont: Biology and Emerging Clinical Relevance.

Authors: Dimitrelou P, Alonaris E, Sergounioti A
Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70584
Published: 2026-Nov-17

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To review the biology of Nanosynbacter lyticus strain TM7x and critically assess its proposed relevance to periodontal disease. METHODS: This narrative review integrates foundational cultivation studies with a targeted PubMed update conducted on 29 October 2026. Human observational findings are distinguished from experimental evidence and from results concerning other Saccharibacteria. RESULTS: TM7x is an ultrasmall, genome-reduced episymbiont whose replication requires a compatible bacterial host. Studies of its interaction with Schaalia odontolytica XH001 reveal host adaptation, specialised pili, metabolic activity during transmission and changes in host physiology. Human disease associations frequently concern broader Saccharibacteria taxa and vary with population, sampling site and analytical method. Experimental studies demonstrate reduced inflammatory responses and, for several epibiont-host pairs, reduced bone loss in mice. These effects are context-dependent and do not establish clinical protection. Detailed knowledge of the species remains concentrated on the reference strain. CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence does not establish TM7x as a causative human periodontal pathogen. It supports a model of context-dependent microbial and immune modulation, with unresolved consequences for human disease.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE(S): To develop and validate an artificial intelligence (AI) system for standardized Ni classification of nasopharyngeal narrow-band imaging (NBI) and to evaluate whether AI assistance improves physician diagnostic consistency and biopsy-related decision making in a reader-study setting. METHODS: In this multicenter diagnostic study, 5404 high-quality nasopharyngeal NBI images were retrospectively collected. item.title: Mitomycin C/5-Fluorouracil Versus Cisplatin/5-Fluorouracil With Hyperfractionated Accelerated Radiotherapy in Locally Advanced Head and Neck Cancer: The ARO 04-01/AHMO Trial.

Abstract:
PURPOSE: Cisplatin-based concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CRT) is the standard for locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). For cisplatin (CDDP)-ineligible patients, mitomycin C/5-fluorouracil (MMC/5-FU) is the most common alternative, but randomized comparisons are lacking. We compared MMC/5-FU with CDDP/5-FU as concurrent partners of hyperfractionated-accelerated radiotherapy (HART) in unresectable, locally advanced HNSCC. PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this multicenter phase III trial, 364 patients with stage IVA/IVB (UICC TNM 6th edition) oropharyngeal or hypopharyngeal HNSCC were randomized 1:1 to HART (72 Gy/6 weeks) plus either weekly CDDP 30 mg/m² (n=182) or MMC 10 mg/m² on days 5 and 36 (n=182), both with continuous-infusion 5-FU 600 mg/m²/d on days 1-5. The primary endpoint was overall survival (OS); secondary endpoints included freedom from progression (FFP), freedom from distant metastasis (FFDM), local, regional and locoregional control, and toxicity, analyzed by Kaplan-Meier and, post hoc, in a competing-risk framework. RESULTS: After a median follow-up of 87 months, CDDP/5-FU was not superior for OS (10-year OS 23% vs. 18%; hazard ratio [HR] 0.89, 95% CI 0.69-1.15; log-rank p=0.418). In the competing-risk analysis, CDDP/5-FU reduced distant metastasis (5-year cumulative incidence 25.9% vs. 36.1%; subdistribution HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.45-0.96; p=0.031) and progression (45.6% vs. 56.3%; subdistribution HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.55-0.98; p=0.037). Kaplan-Meier estimates were directionally consistent but not significant (10-year FFDM 66% vs. 52%; HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.48-1.02; p=0.060; FFP HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.59-1.05); local, regional and locoregional control (HR 0.80-1.01) and toxicity profiles did not differ. Serum creatinine (p<0.001) and the AE/SAE rate (24.2% vs. 15.4%; p=0.048) were higher with CDDP. CONCLUSION: ARO 04-01/AHMO did not show superiority of CDDP/5-FU over MMC/5-FU for overall survival. Abstract:
PURPOSE/OBJECTIVES: MnTnBuOE-2-PyP5+ (BMX-001) is a manganese metalloporphyrin superoxide dismutase mimic that inhibits radiation stress-induced pathways and may mitigate treatment-related side effects. We evaluated the safety and efficacy of BMX-001 on severe oral mucositis (OM), xerostomia, dermatitis, quality of life, and patient reported outcomes (PROs) among patients undergoing chemoradiation for head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). MATERIALS/METHODS: This multicenter, phase I/II trial included patients with stage III-IVB HNSCC (AJCC 7th ed) undergoing definitive or postoperative chemoradiation (CRT). Patients received a subcutaneous BMX-001 loading dose followed by twice-weekly maintenance dosing through one week post-CRT at three loading/maintenance dose levels (7/3.5 mg, 14/7 mg, and 28/14 mg), with level 3 expanded for phase II endpoints. OM, xerostomia, and dermatitis were assessed weekly during treatment, within one month, and at six and 12 months post-chemoradiation. PROs and saliva production (stimulated and unstimulated) were measured at baseline, end of CRT, and one, six and 12 months post-CRT. Descriptive statistics summarized adverse events, symptom duration, and PROs. RESULTS: Between 5/2017 and 12/2019, 29 patients were enrolled; 86% had oropharynx primaries (n=25; n=24 HPV+) and 89.7% (n=26) underwent definitive CRT. One patient experienced two serious adverse events possibly related to BMX-001. Grade 3 OM occurred in 41.4% (n=12); acute and chronic grade ≥2 xerostomia occurred in 17.9% (n=5) and 9.1% (n=2), respectively, and 6.9% (n=2) experienced grade 3 dermatitis. Several measures were no longer statistically different from baseline by six months, while measures of xerostomia remained elevated. CONCLUSIONS: BMX-001 is safe and feasible in patients with advanced HNSCC. In addition, BMX-001 shows promising efficacy for mitigating CRT-associated toxicity and warrants further study in larger, controlled trials.

item.title: Neoadjuvant talazoparib, irinotecan, and standard chemotherapy for early breast cancer in the I-SPY2 trial.
item.dc:creator: Clark AS, Omene C, Yau C, Wallace AM, Stringer-Reasor E, Chien AJ, Isaacs C, Han HS, Albain KS, Boughey JC, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Clark AS, Omene C, Yau C, Wallace AM, Stringer-Reasor E, Chien AJ, Isaacs C, Han HS, Albain KS, Boughey JC, et al.
Journal: ESMO open | DOI: 10.1016/j.esmoop.2026.108643
Published: 2026-Nov-17

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preclinical evidence suggests synergy between poly-ADP-ribose inhibitors and camptothecin chemotherapy. We tested the talazoparib and irinotecan combination (TI) in the neoadjuvant setting in the I-SPY2 trial in patients with HER2-negative locally advanced breast cancer. MATERIALS AND METHODS: I-SPY2 is a phase II platform trial for stage 2/3 early breast cancer at high risk of recurrence. Participants were adaptively randomized to one of several experimental neoadjuvant therapies or control based on receptor subtypes defined by hormone receptor (HR), HER2 status, and MammaPrint risk (MP1, MP2). The primary endpoint was pathological complete response (pCR). Treatments 'graduate' if/when they achieve an 85% Bayesian probability of success in a subtype-specific phase III trial. Only HER2-negative patients were eligible for randomization to the TI arm. All patients received weekly paclitaxel for 12 weeks, followed by doxorubicin/cyclophosphamide and surgery. Participants randomized to the TI arm received daily oral talazoparib and irinotecan infusions every other week. Pathway-specific biomarkers were assessed for response prediction. RESULTS: The combination of talazoparib and irinotecan failed to graduate from the I-SPY2 trial, with a 19% modeled posterior probability of pCR in the TI arm compared with 20% in the control arm among all patients with HER2-negative breast cancer. item.title: Prevalence and associated factors of influenza A virus infection among patients with acute respiratory tract infections in Gondar City, Northwest Ethiopia.

item.description:
Authors: Asamnew A, Shure W, Asres MS, Wondimeneh Y, Ferede G, Gelaw B, Gelaw A
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0357953
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43043898



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Influenza A virus is a major cause of acute respiratory tract infections and contributes substantially to the global disease burden. Laboratory-confirmed data on influenza A virus infection remain limited in the study area. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the prevalence of influenza A virus infection and to identify possible associated factors among patients with acute respiratory tract infections attending selected health institutions in Gondar City, Northwest Ethiopia. METHODS: A multi-center, health facility-based cross-sectional study was carried out from January 1, 2025 to December 31, 2025. In total, 490 patients with acute respiratory tract infections were enrolled from five health facilities in Gondar City. Demographic, behavioral, and clinical information was collected using a structured questionnaire. Nasopharyngeal swabs were collected and tested for influenza A virus using multiplex real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). Logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with influenza A virus infection. RESULTS: Influenza A virus was detected in 65 of the 490 participants, with an overall prevalence of 13.3% (95% CI: 10.3-16.3). Among the confirmed cases, 48 (73.8%) were A(H1N1) and 17 (26.2%) were A(H3N2). In multivariable logistic regression, participants aged 5-17 years (AOR: 3.14; 95% CI: 1.36-7.25; p = 0.008) and 18-49 years (AOR: 3.50; 95% CI: 1.54-7.20; p = 0.002) had higher odds of infection than those aged <5 years. Secondary education was associated with lower odds of infection compared with no formal education (AOR: 0.07; 95% CI: 0.01-0.75; p = 0.029), while employed participants had higher odds than students (AOR: 3.54; 95% CI: 1.47-7.80; p = 0.028). CONCLUSION: Influenza A virus infection was detected among patients presenting with acute respiratory tract infections in Gondar City, highlighting the importance of influenza surveillance and laboratory confirmation in this population. Strengthening routine molecular surveillance, promoting seasonal influenza vaccination among high-risk populations, reinforcing infection prevention and control measures, and implementing targeted community health education are essential to improve influenza prevention and control.

item.title: Age as a determinant of trampoline-related oral-facial-head injuries in pediatric emergency department visits: A NEISS analysis.

Authors: Wiener RC, Waters C

Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43043884



Abstract:
Over the last decade trampoline use has increased. Many injuries occur that require emergency department (ED) care. The purpose of this research is to examine the role of age in trampoline-related oral-facial-head injuries that require ED care. Data from the 2024 National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS) was used. Trampoline-related injuries were extracted from the data set. Oral-facial-head trampoline-related injuries were compared with other types of trampoline-related injuries by age groups (0 to <6 years, 6 to <12 years, and 12 to ≤18 years) in Chi-Square analyses and logistic regression analyses. There were 3548 NEISS-reported trampoline-associated injuries for children, ages 0 to ≤18 years, in 2024. This corresponded to an estimated 101,474 trampoline injuries in the United States in 2024. Of these, 21.7% were oral-facial-head trampoline-related injuries (weighted estimate of 22,033 injuries). Of all the trampoline-related injuries in children ages 0 to ≤18 years, children ages 0 to <6 years had 33.0% of the injuries; children ages 6 to <12 years had 51.9%; and, children ages 12 to ≤18 years had 15.1%. These findings highlight the need for targeted prevention and anticipatory guidance for younger children.

item.title: ERBB2 amplification and salivary-gland-enriched residual non-ICI scenario-based genomic signal coverage in head and neck cancer comprehensive genomic profiling: a nationwide C-CAT analysis.

Abstract:
PURPOSE: Comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) in head and neck cancer can return tumor-agnostic and histology-associated signals, but practical benchmarks for reported ERBB2 amplification and residual non-immune-checkpoint-inhibitor (non-ICI) scenario-based genomic signal coverage are limited. METHODS: This retrospective descriptive scenario-based analysis included anonymized C-CAT-derived head and neck CGP-tested cases. Overall and residual non-ICI frameworks were assessed before ERBB2, after adding reported ERBB2 amplification, and after adding ALK fusion/rearrangement as an updated 2026 layer. RESULTS: The cohort included 3,089 cases. In the overall framework, scenario-based genomic signal coverage increased from 280/3,089 (9.1%) to 501/3,089 (16.2%) after adding reported ERBB2 amplification (+ 221 cases; +7.2% points). ALK fusion/rearrangement added 0 cases. CONCLUSION: Reported ERBB2 amplification materially increased scenario-based genomic signal coverage in head and neck cancer, especially salivary duct carcinoma. item.title: Molecular Residual Disease After Definitive Chemoradiotherapy in Locally Advanced Head and Neck Cancer: Clinical Value and Optimal Timing for ctDNA Assessment.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate post-treatment assessment after definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT) in locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (LA-HNSCC) remains challenging due to limitations of standard imaging. RESULTS: Baseline ctDNA was detectable in 85.1% of patients. item.title: Positive Surgical Margins in Sinonasal Cancer: A Contemporary Analysis of Risk Factors and Survival.
item.dc:creator: Fu BJ, Moon P, Lee JJ, Ayoub NF

Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71066

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sinonasal cancers (SNCs) are rare, aggressive malignancies in which surgery remains a cornerstone of multimodal treatment. Contemporary national data on positive surgical margins (PSM), risk factors, and survival implications are limited. We evaluated temporal trends, predictors, and prognostic significance of PSMs in SNC. METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study using the National Cancer Database (2015-2022). Adults with cT1-4bN0M0 SNC undergoing definitive surgery were included; those with unknown tumor size, prior malignancy, or missing margin status were excluded. RESULTS: The final cohort included 753 patients (mean age 63.4 years [SD 11.8]; 33.2% female). PSMs occurred in 253 patients (33.6%), increasing from 29.6% in 2015 to 41.8% in 2022 (adjusted OR 1.09/year, 95% CI 1.02-1.17). Independent predictors included cT3-T4b stage (aRR 1.53, 95% CI 1.09-2.13), maxillary sinus origin (aRR 1.54, 95% CI 1.22-1.96), Charlson-Deyo score ≥ 3 (aRR 1.42, 95% CI 1.01-1.99), conversion to open surgery (aRR 2.01, 95% CI 1.14-3.55), and Native American race (aRR 2.92, 95% CI 1.65-5.18). CONCLUSIONS: PSMs remain common in SNC, increasing over time and independently predicting worse survival. Efforts to refine surgical techniques and multidisciplinary, histology-guided treatment strategies may improve oncologic outcomes.

item.title: EUSICA/INSICA Position Paper on Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Nasal Vestibule: A Distinct Clinical Entity Requiring Dedicated Classification, Treatment Strategies and Outcome Measures.

item.description:

Published: 2026-Nov-16

Abstract:
PURPOSE: Cancer of the nasal vestibule (CNV) differs anatomically and clinically from both sinonasal and cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, yet lacks formal recognition as a separate clinical entity and topographical subsite; whether it is also biologically distinct has not yet been investigated. EUSICA/INSICA advocates for formal recognition of CNV and a unified classification, treatment, and translational framework. METHOD: Published literature on CNV, including population-based cohorts, T-classification studies, brachytherapy outcomes, and quality-of-life data, was reviewed by an international multidisciplinary EUSICA/INSICA expert panel to formulate consensus recommendations. FINDING: CNV shows favorable outcomes, drains preferentially to facial and submandibular nodes, and is amenable to organ-preserving radiotherapy, in particular brachytherapy. It is staged using four non-uniform systems; multicenter validation in 609 patients from 21 centers supported the prognostic utility of the New Rome classification integrated with clinical nodal status. Validated CNV-specific quality-of-life instruments are lacking. Compared with NCCN-defined high-risk cutaneous SCC of the nose, CNV differs in topography, pattern of local spread, prognostic landmarks, nodal behavior, and treatment paradigm. Comparative molecular data versus cutaneous and sinonasal SCC are not yet available. CONCLUSION: EUSICA/INSICA calls for formal recognition of CNV as a distinct ICD-O-3 subsite, incorporation of the New Rome T classification into UICC/AJCC TNM, standardized organ-preserving treatment, and dedicated translational research, including comparative molecular studies to determine whether its clinical distinctness has a biological basis.

item.title: Exploring the Financial Toxicity and Opportunity Costs of Smoking in Lung and Head and Neck Cancer.
item.dc:creator: Stemme RA, Najjar W, Armache M, Lababidi G, Samaha NL, Kacker S, Gentsch AT, Gharzai LA, Galiatsatos P, St John MA, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Stemme RA, Najjar W, Armache M, Lababidi G, Samaha NL, Kacker S, Gentsch AT, Gharzai LA, Galiatsatos P, St John MA, et al.
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71065
Published: 2026-Nov-16

Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Patients with lung and head and neck cancers (L/HNC) face disproportionately high rates of financial toxicity (FT) and persistent smoking after diagnosis, yet the relationship between tobacco use, associated spending, and FT remains poorly understood. This study characterizes this relationship in patients with L/HNC. METHODS: We conducted a mixed-methods study with semi-structured interviews from 03/2024 to 03/2025 and data analyzed from 07/2024 to 11/2025. Patients with newly diagnosed L/HNC were enrolled through convenience sampling. Transcripts were analyzed using content analysis until thematic saturation. Participants completed the Comprehensive Score for Financial Toxicity (COST) (11-items; 0-44, lower scores represent worse FT), USDA Six-Item Short Form Food Security Module, and smoking-induced deprivation (SID) questionnaire to assess psychosocial, material, and behavioral FT components, respectively. RESULTS: Among 25 participants (13 [52%]) male; 18 (72%) non-Hispanic White; median age 61 years (range, 44-78 years)], 12 (48%) were current smokers at diagnosis. Median COST score was 21 (range 4-43), with 15 (63%) experiencing FT (COST < 26). Eight (33%) patients reported food insecurity. Participants spent a median of $155 (IQR $63-$285) monthly on cigarettes, and 4 (17%) reported SID. Qualitative analysis confirmed an established FT framework and identified tobacco use and spending as a bidirectional contributor to FT. CONCLUSIONS: Tobacco use and spending have a bidirectional relationship with FT, contributing to FT across the material, psychosocial, and behavioral domains, while serving as a coping mechanism for financial distress. Our findings underscore the need for integrated smoking cessation and FT interventions alongside targeted FT screening for patients with a smoking history.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic significance of young age in squamous cell carcinoma of the mobile tongue and floor of mouth remains controversial. We compared clinicopathological characteristics and oncologic outcomes between young and older patients undergoing surgery. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included patients treated with primary curative-intent surgery at 13 high-volume European cancer centers between 2012 and 2022. Patients were stratified as young (≤40 years) or older (≥55 years); those aged 41-54 years were excluded. Clinicopathological variables, recurrence, overall survival (OS), and disease-specific survival (DSS) were compared. RESULTS: Among 375 patients, 133 were young and 242 older. Younger patients were more often never smokers (67.2% vs 47.5%; p = 0.001), non-drinkers (95.1% vs 74.5%; p < 0.001), and had early pT disease (62.9% vs 48.3%; p = 0.009) and lower tumor grade (p = 0.041). Pathological nodal involvement, lymphovascular invasion, perineural invasion, and extranodal extension were comparable. Younger patients had higher odds of positive margins (18.3% vs 10.5%; OR 1.898; p = 0.034). In advanced pT disease, perineural invasion was more frequent in younger patients (71.4% vs 54.5%; p = 0.042). OS, DSS, and recurrence did not differ significantly between groups. After adjustment for pT, pN, tobacco exposure, and alcohol consumption, age was not associated with OS or DSS. CONCLUSIONS: Young adults show lower tobacco and alcohol exposure and more favorable local tumor features without improved oncologic outcomes. Young age should not be considered an inherently favorable prognostic factor. Further translational studies are warranted to clarify the biological mechanisms underlying early-onset disease.

item.title: Struggling minds in lower ranks: Stronger ACC-OFC-amygdala coupling despite reduced selection of effortful options in subordinate male rats.
item.dc:creator: Roshani G, Heysieattalab S, Farkhondeh Tale Navi F
item.description:
Authors: Roshani G, Heysieattalab S, Farkhondeh Tale Navi F
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0362370
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43038302



Abstract:
Social hierarchy can influence how individuals allocate effort to obtain rewards, but the neural mechanisms underlying rank-related differences in effort-based decision-making remain unclear. We investigated whether social rank is associated with effort-based choice and local and interregional neural activity in male rats. Twenty-one male Wistar rats were classified as dominant, intermediate, or subordinate based on repeated tube-test performance. Rats then performed a T-maze effort-based decision-making task in which they chose between a high-reward/high-effort option (six food pellets with a 30-cm barrier) and a low-reward/no-effort option (two food pellets without a barrier). Local field potentials were recorded from the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), orbitofrontal cortex (OFC), and amygdala (AM). Dominant rats selected the high-reward/high-effort option more frequently than intermediate and subordinate rats, whereas response latency did not differ significantly among social-rank groups. Subordinate rats exhibited greater theta and high-gamma power in the ACC, OFC, and AM, as well as greater low-beta power in selected regions. Interregional coherence differed across social-rank groups in a frequency- and pathway-specific manner. Subordinate rats generally showed greater low-beta and high-gamma coherence in the OFC-AM, OFC-ACC, and ACC-AM pathways, whereas dominant rats showed greater theta coherence in the OFC-ACC and ACC-AM pathways. Several associations between neural measures and choice behavior were observed, particularly for low-beta and high-gamma activity and coherence, although these relationships varied across social-rank groups and neural pathways. These findings indicate that social rank is associated with differences in effort-based choice and with frequency- and pathway-specific alterations in ACC-OFC-AM neural dynamics. Overall, the findings suggest that social experience and hierarchical position are associated with distinct patterns of cortical-limbic activity during effort-based decision-making.

item.title: Impact of nicotine concentration, form, and stereoisomer ratio on oral nicotine pouch pharmacokinetics and abuse liability: Protocol for a randomized crossover study in adults who use tobacco.
item.dc:creator: Tomko PM, Cho YJ, Curran H, Hinton A, Wagener TL, Brinkman MC, Keller-Hamilton B
item.description:
Authors: Tomko PM, Cho YJ, Curran H, Hinton A, Wagener TL, Brinkman MC, Keller-Hamilton B
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0362198
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43038220



Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Oral nicotine pouches (ONPs) are tobacco-free products placed between the lip and gum to deliver nicotine. Sales have grown rapidly in the United States (U.S.), yet independent data on how nicotine characteristics shape ONP appeal and addiction potential are lacking. Three nicotine characteristics vary across ONPs: concentration (mass of nicotine per pouch), form (the fraction of freebase, or unprotonated, nicotine), and stereoisomer (the proportion of S- to R-nicotine). This study will determine how these characteristics independently and jointly affect ONP nicotine pharmacokinetics and user experience among adults who smoke cigarettes or use moist snuff. DESIGN AND PARTICIPANTS: This randomized, double-blind, crossover trial will enroll 160 adults who smoke cigarettes or use moist snuff at a single U.S. site. INTERVENTIONS AND OUTCOMES: Participants will be randomized 1:1 to a lower (3 mg) or higher (6 mg) nicotine concentration arm. Within each arm, participants will complete five laboratory sessions in balanced, randomized order: four standardized ONP sessions (30 minutes, with the pouch placed between lip and gum) varying by nicotine form (30% vs. 70% freebase) and stereoisomer ratio (racemic [50% R- and 50% S-nicotine] vs. > 99% S-nicotine), plus one session using their usual tobacco product. Sessions will be separated by at least 48 hours. The primary outcome is maximum plasma nicotine concentration (Cmax). Secondary outcomes include time to maximum concentration (Tmax), total nicotine absorbed over 90 minutes (AUC), subjective effects, and behavioral economic demand indices. CONCLUSIONS: This will be the first study to systematically examine how nicotine concentration, form, and stereoisomer ratio interact to influence ONP abuse liability. Findings will identify which product characteristics drive ONP addiction potential and will inform FDA regulation aimed at maximizing the potential for ONPs to serve as a harm reduction alternative to cigarettes and moist snuff.
