item.title: Innovative mHealth intervention providing sustained anticipatory guidance (zero cavity): Design, validation, user perception and effectiveness - A randomized controlled trial protocol.
item.dc:creator: Murugan SM, Dhar V, Saikia A, Sampath V, Ramendran H, Balakrishnan K, Nirmal L, Pasupathy U, Davis J
item.description:
Authors: Murugan SM, Dhar V, Saikia A, Sampath V, Ramendran H, Balakrishnan K, Nirmal L, Pasupathy U, Davis J
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0359152
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43038214



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Early Childhood Caries (ECC) remains one of the most common chronic conditions in childhood, affecting over 600 million children globally. When untreated, it can lead to severe pain, abscesses, difficulty in chewing that contributes to malnutrition, impaired speech, disrupted sleep, low self-esteem, social withdrawal, and poor academic performance, all of which diminish a child's overall quality of life. Although largely preventable, ECC remains highly prevalent because of delayed preventive care and low parental awareness. Effective health education needs to be consistent, accessible, and available whenever parents need it. Although current evidence indicates that anticipatory guidance is a proven approach, its long-term reinforcement through a mobile app has not yet been tested. This study aims to develop and evaluate the effectiveness of a mobile health (mHealth) application delivering Sustained Anticipatory Guidance (SAG) for the prevention of ECC. METHODS AND ANALYSIS: A two-arm parallel hospital-based randomized controlled trial will be conducted at Sri Ramachandra Institute of Higher Education & Research, Chennai, India. The study will enrol 540 mother-infant dyads from the departments of Pediatric Medicine and the Centre for Early Childhood Caries Research (CECCRe). Eligible dyads with infants aged 6-12 months in the predentate stage will be randomized to the "Zero-Cavity" mHealth app (intervention) or standard care (control). Baseline and semi-annual data on oral hygiene, fluoride exposure, and feeding/diet will be collected. Calibrated dentists will perform quarterly clinical exams using ICDAS II criteria, recording cavitated and non-cavitated lesions. For children at high risk or with enamel defects/incipient lesions, clinical photographs will be taken to support individualized preventive guidance. The primary outcome will be the effectiveness of the app in preventing ECC, while the secondary outcomes will include ECC incidence and prevalence. DISCUSSION: Despite being largely preventable, ECC remains a major public health challenge, sustained by limited preventive access and inconsistent counselling, especially in LMICs. This trial evaluates the Zero Cavity app, believed to bridge this gap by providing sustained, age-appropriate anticipatory guidance beyond clinic settings on oral development, hygiene, diet/feeding, and fluoride use. The behavioural theory-driven approach is expected to enhance cultural relevance, usability, and behaviour change, with optimism that process evaluation will illuminate engagement and implementation. It is believed that this large, adequately powered, parallel-group RCT with intention-to-treat analysis will offer, with optimism, a scalable, low-cost model that will expand the reach and consistency of continuous preventive care in diverse urban and peri-urban populations. item.description:
Authors: Nasim MT, Rana NA, Mukhtar U, Sheryar M, Rabia G, Sehar S, Khan MJ, Khan MJ, Awan HM
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0362467
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43038194



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: MicroRNAs fine-tune gene expression and control signaling pathways. When perturbed, they can have serious consequences, such as cancer. Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is the most prevalent form of oral-related malignancies. Among different signaling pathways, the IL-17 pathway is strongly associated with the aggressive course of OSCC. We investigated the expression of a primate-specific miR-548c-3p and its potential association with IL-17 pathway-related genes. AIMS: Study the expression of hsa-miR-548c-3p and its target genes of IL-17 pathway in oral cancer. METHODOLOGY: Bioinformatics analysis was conducted on OSCC microarray datasets to identify dysregulated genes. KEGG pathway analysis was used to identify IL-17 pathway genes. Experimental validation was conducted using RT-qPCR, correlation between miRNA and its putative target genes was conducted using Spearman correlation, and diagnostic accuracy was assessed using ROC analysis. RESULTS: Among the 379 predicted targets of miR-548c-3p, FOSL1 and SRSF1, key genes in the IL-17 pathway, exhibited significant up-regulation in the bioinformatic analysis. Experimental validation confirmed the significant down-regulation of miR-548c-3p alongside a significant up-regulation of SRSF1, where correlation analysis revealed a strong inverse relation between them, whereas FOSL1 showed a non-significant up-regulation and a moderate inverse association with miR-548c-3p. ROC analysis demonstrated strong diagnostic potential for both miR-548c-3p and SRSF1. CONCLUSION: hsa-miR-548c-3p down-regulation is inversely correlated with both IL-17 pathway genes, ROC curve analysis underscores the potential diagnostic biomarker potential of hsa-miR-548c-3p and SRSF1, establishing them as promising therapeutic targets in OSCC.

item.title: Recurrence in chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps: a retrospective surgical cohort study.

Abstract:
PURPOSE: To assess the association of endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS) strategy with the frequency and timing of postoperative recurrence in chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP), using prespecified clinical-endoscopic criteria. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study with 3-year follow-up was conducted in CRSwNP patients who underwent ESS. Surgical procedures were classified according to the Lamella Ostium Extent Mucosa (LOEM) system (t1-t4). Postoperative recurrence was defined by symptom worsening and/or endoscopic evidence of polyp relapse. Logistic regression identified independent predictors of recurrence, while Kaplan-Meier and Cox models assessed recurrence-free survival. A Cox-derived prognostic index, based on the model linear predictor, was used to stratify patients into risk groups. RESULTS: In the overall sample (n = 172), 38.4% of patients met recurrence criteria, with rates varying across LOEM groups. Extensive ESS (t3-t4) was associated with significantly lower recurrence risk (OR = 0.10 and 0.28) and longer recurrence-free survival (HR = 0.51, p = 0.038). Exploratory subgroup Cox analyses identified nominally significant associations with lower recurrence hazards in patients with asthma (HR = 0.21), N-ERD (HR = 0.28), atopy (HR = 0.25) and total IgE > 100 (HR = 0.22), with similar patterns in women, surgery-naive and delayed-ESS cases. Prognostic stratification showed a clear gradient in recurrence burden from 12.1% to 58.6% across risk groups, with higher-risk strata displaying a progressively more unfavorable type 2 inflammatory profile and greater baseline disease burden. CONCLUSION: Surgical extent was associated with both recurrence risk and timing. Extensive ESS (t3-t4) was associated with more sustained disease control, with exploratory signals in selected type 2-associated profiles. These findings support further investigation of individualized surgical strategies, although further studies are needed.

item.title: Hypoactive APOBEC3A Achieves High-Level Mutagenesis and Drives Squamous Cell Carcinoma.

Abstract:
APOBEC proteins shape the somatic mutation spectrum of many cancers by binding and editing DNA. Modeling APOBEC-induced changes in cancer has been challenging due to the toxicity of these enzymes. Here, we overcame this barrier using a mutant form of APOBEC3A with impaired deaminase activity by changing arginine 128 to alanine (A3AR128A). Overexpressing A3AR128A in murine epithelium induced squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) in the skin, head and neck region, and cervix, mirroring the human disease spectrum. Tumor formation was further accelerated by concomitant Trp53 loss. A3AR128A cancers carried frequent alterations in the NOTCH and RAS-PI3K pathways, and recurrent mutations in genes encoding histone H3 were also observed. Cross-species analysis revealed how APOBEC accessibility influences cancer driver gene selection. A catalogue of 235,790 mutations was used to refine mutational signatures linked to A3A. These results shed light on how DNA damage from A3A contributes to tumorigenesis.

item.title: Optimizing Induction Chemotherapy in Locally Advanced Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma: A Risk-Stratified Recursive Partitioning Analysis Based on 9th Edition Staging.
item.dc:creator: Lin J, Wang T, Xiao J, Lin J, Liu T, Lu J, Mo H, Xie R, Mai H, Chen Q
item.description:
Authors: Lin J, Wang T, Xiao J, Lin J, Liu T, Lu J, Mo H, Xie R, Mai H, Chen Q
Journal: International journal of cancer | DOI: 10.1002/ijc.70819
Published: 2026-Nov-16

Abstract:
Although induction chemotherapy (IC) in combination with concurrent chemoradiotherapy constitutes the standard treatment for locally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma (LANPC), the optimal number of IC cycles remains undetermined. The 9th edition staging system provides a refined risk stratification framework. We aimed to develop a prognostic tool to stratify patients with LANPC and define the optimal number of IC cycles for distinct risk groups based on new staging. We analyzed 1216 patients with LANPC treated with IC and employed propensity score matching to minimize bias. Progression-free survival (PFS) was the primary endpoint, analyzed using Kaplan-Meier curves. A recursive partitioning analysis (RPA) model was developed and validated for risk stratification. Survival outcomes and toxicities were compared across IC cycle groups. After a median follow-up of 56 months, 2- and 3-cycle IC yielded greater improvements in PFS compared with 4-cycle IC (p < 0.001). The RPA model incorporated 9th edition staging, pretreatment EBV DNA, and IC response, stratifying patients into three risk categories. For low-risk patients, 2- and 3-cycle IC yielded comparable PFS, both superior to 4-cycle IC (p < 0.001). In intermediate-risk patients, significantly higher 5-year PFS was achieved with 2-cycle IC than with 3- (73.4% vs. 56.2%, p = 0.014) or 4-cycle IC (73.4% vs. 47.5%, p < 0.001). High-risk patients benefited more from 3-cycle versus 2- (47.5% vs. 31.7%; p = 0.038) or 4-cycle IC (47.5% vs. 36.2%; p = 0.039). Overall, the RPA-based model effectively stratified risk, guiding individualized IC cycle selection. Balancing toxicity and efficacy, 2-cycle IC is optimal for the low- and intermediate-risk groups, while 3-cycle IC is preferred for the high-risk group.

item.title: Prognostic Predictors in Patients With Necrotizing Otitis Externa: A Retrospective Cohort Study.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Necrotizing otitis externa (NOE) is a rare infection with a heterogeneous clinical course that complicates prognostication. The impact of diabetes mellitus on outcomes remains controversial, and objective predictors of treatment duration are unclear. This study aimed to identify the factors associated with prolonged hospitalization in patients with NOE. STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective observational study. SETTING: Tertiary academic medical center. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 61 patients with NOE admitted between September 2009 and October 2024. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, microbiological, and radiological data, as well as length of hospital stay, were analyzed. Magnetic resonance imaging assessed skull-base osteomyelitis and white matter lesions using the Fazekas scale. Multivariable linear regression identified factors associated with hospital stay. RESULTS: The mean age was 70.25 ± 13.11 years (63.9% male; mean hospital stay 46.02 ± 37.50 days). Diabetes was present in 75.4% of the patients, but neither diabetes nor hemoglobin A1c levels were associated with hospital stay. In the univariate analysis, diabetic complications, external auditory canal swelling, cranial nerve palsy, peak inflammatory marker levels, inflammatory marker normalization times, and higher Fazekas scores were associated with prolonged hospitalization, whereas only diabetic complications and higher Fazekas scores remained independently associated in the multivariable analysis (adjusted R2 = 0.425). CONCLUSION: Diabetic complications and higher Fazekas scores were independently associated with prolonged hospitalization in patients with NOE. These findings suggest that chronic microvascular disease burden, rather than conventional vascular risk factors alone, may contribute to a prolonged disease course. Further prospective multicenter studies are needed to validate these findings.

item.title: Evaluating the Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index for Predicting Outcomes Following Head and Neck Free-Flap Reconstruction.

Published: 2026-Nov-16

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Malnutrition has been associated with adverse outcomes among head and neck cancer (HNC) patients. Despite this, there is no universally accepted standard for screening of nutrition-related risk. This study aimed to determine if nutrition-related risk, as defined by the Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index (GNRI), is associated with adverse postoperative outcomes following microvascular free tissue transfer (MFTT) for HNC. STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study. SETTING: Population-based study using the 2010 to 2022 American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (ACS-NSQIP). METHODS: Patients aged >65 years who underwent MFTT for HNC were stratified into 3 cohorts based on preoperative GNRI: no nutrition-related risk (GNRI > 98), moderate nutrition-related risk (GNRI 92-98), and major nutrition-related risk (GNRI < 92). After adjusting for potential confounders, multivariable logistic regression models were performed to assess the association between GNRI and postoperative outcomes. RESULTS: Of 1586 patients, 945 (59.6%) patients had a GNRI corresponding with no nutrition-related risk, 346 (21.8%) had moderate nutrition-related risk, and 295 (18.6%) had major nutrition-related risk. On multivariable regression, both moderate and major nutrition-related risk cohorts were associated with surgical, medical, and Clavien-Dindo grade IV (CDIV) complications, along with non-home discharge, respectively (P < .05). Prospective studies are needed to validate the utility of the GNRI as a preoperative risk stratification tool to optimize surgical outcomes following MFTT for HNC.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study examined the global burden of early-onset nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). STUDY DESIGN: Data on early-onset NPC patients aged 15 to 49 years from 1990 to 2021 were from GBD 2021 to evaluate disease burden and forecast to 2050. SETTING: Early-onset NPC patients aged 15 to 49 years; Global Burden of Disease (GBD) database 2021; period 1990 to 2021. METHODS: The burden of NPC was evaluated using incidence, mortality, disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs), sociodemographic index (SDI), and average annual percentage change (AAPC). Changes in risk factors affecting NPC were also analyzed. Bayesian age-period-cohort analysis was applied to forecast the disease burden spanning 2022 to 2050. RESULTS: Globally, the incidence, mortality, and DALYs of early-onset NPC all declined during 1990 to 2021. The AAPC of incidence, mortality, and DALYs were -0.32 (95% CI: -0.39 to -0.26), -2.12 (-2.16 to -2.08), and -2.09 (-2.13 to -2.05), respectively. The DALYs for NPC exhibited a markedly declining trend among various SDI regions over the 1990-2021 period. East Asia [AAPC: -3.19 (-3.26 to -3.12)] and Western Europe [AAPC: -3.04 (-3.16 to -2.96)] experienced the largest drops in DALYs from 1990 to 2021. High alcohol consumption, smoking, and formaldehyde exposure were major contributing factors to DALYs for early-onset NPC, with no significant changes observed between 1990 and 2021. From 2022 to 2050, the disease burden of early-onset NPC worldwide is projected to decline. CONCLUSIONS: Globally, the burden of early-onset NPC declined during 1990 to 2021 period and is projected to continue to decline in the future.

item.title: Fine motor impairment in long-term survivors of nasopharyngeal carcinoma after intensity-modulated radiotherapy.

Published: 2026-Nov-15

Abstract:
PURPOSE: Characterize fine motor outcomes among nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) survivors and associated clinical and radiation dose factors. METHODS: We enrolled 190 NPC survivors at a median of 7.0 years (range, 1.0-13.6) after definitive intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT); 86.3 % (164/190) received concurrent chemotherapy. Fine motor function was evaluated using Grooved Pegboard Test (GP) Z-scores normalized to age and educational level. Motor-related regions of interest (ROIs), including bilateral precentral and postcentral gyri, thalami, striata, cerebella, brain stem, and spinal cord, were segmented in 105 patients for dosimetric analyses. RESULTS: NPC survivors exhibited significant bilateral fine motor impairment compared with normative data (median GP Z-score, -0.3; p < 0.001); 22.1 % (42/190) and 18.9 % (36/190) of patients scored ≥ 2 standard deviations below norms for their dominant and nondominant hands respectively. Advanced T-category was associated with higher radiation doses to motor ROIs and poorer GP Z-scores in both dominant (p < 0.001) and nondominant hands (p = 0.014). Higher Dmax and D1 % to the precentral gyri were associated with poorer GP Z-scores in the corresponding hands. High cumulative cisplatin exposure was associated with worse motor performance in both hands (dominant, p < 0.001; nondominant, p = 0.028); patients who received 450-600 mg/m2 had GP Z-scores equivalent to 43 years of age-related motor dexterity decline compared with those receiving 0-<150 mg/m2. CONCLUSIONS: NPC survivors demonstrated substantial long-term fine motor impairment associated with T-category, radiation dose to the precentral gyri, and cumulative cisplatin exposure. These findings highlight the importance of personalized treatment to minimize neurotoxicity, and long-term fine motor monitoring and rehabilitation for NPC survivors.

item.title: Oral Cancer Screening in the Landscape of Randomized Controlled Trials: A Scoping Review.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To identify the types of cancer and the corresponding screening methods evaluated in randomized controlled trials (RCTs), with a primary focus on situating oral cancer screening within the RCT-based body of evidence. METHODS: This review followed the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Scopus, LILACS, ProQuest, and Google Scholar were searched without date restrictions for studies in English, Spanish, or Portuguese. Eligible studies were RCTs primarily evaluating cancer screening methods (clinical, imaging, endoscopic, laboratory, molecular/serological, or self-examination). Data were synthesized as means and frequencies. RESULTS: Nine cancer types and 33 distinct screening methods were identified across 97 cancer screenings in 91 RCTs spanning 57 years. Oral cancer ranked last, with only one RCT evaluating a single method, oral visual inspection, the fewest of any cancer type. By comparison, colorectal cancer was the most frequently investigated (n = 22/22.7%), followed by breast cancer (n = 21/21.6%) and lung cancer (n = 18/18.6%), with five, six, and four screening methods evaluated, respectively. CONCLUSION: These findings map the RCT landscape in cancer screening, revealing marked disparities in evidence across cancer types and identifying oral cancer as the most limited. Further RCTs are urgently needed to strengthen the evidence base and support effective oral cancer screening programs.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fibrinogen-like protein 1 (FGL1) is involved in tumor progression and immune regulation, but its role in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) is unclear. METHODS: Plasma FGL1 levels were measured in 120 LSCC patients and 50 controls using ELISA. Tissue expression was analyzed via TCGA-HNSC. Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The role of specialist palliative care (SPC) alongside immunotherapy in head and neck cancer (HNC) is unclear. METHODS: This retrospective population-based cohort study included adults with HNC who died in 2013-2021 in Alberta, Canada. The primary exposure was SPC timing (early, late, none), with immunotherapy use in the last 12 months of life as a secondary exposure. The outcome was potentially avoidable acute care use (ICU admission, 15+ hospital days, or 2+ ED visits) in the last month of life. Multivariable logistic regression was performed. RESULTS: Of 1415 patients, 35.3%, 36.7%, and 28.0% received early, late, and no SPC, respectively, while 6.9% received immunotherapy. Early SPC was associated with 40% (95% CI 17%-57%) lower odds of potentially avoidable acute care use, while immunotherapy use was not associated with this outcome (p-value = 0.91). CONCLUSION: Early SPC was associated with lower potentially avoidable acute care use for HNC regardless of immunotherapy use.

Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71062
Published: 2026-Nov-15

Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Buccinator myomucosal flaps (BMF) are increasingly used for reconstruction of small- to medium-sized intraoral defects because they replace oral mucosa with similar tissue. However, donor-site morbidity and its determinants remain poorly defined. This study aimed to evaluate donor-site morbidity after BMF harvest and identify factors associated with unfavorable outcomes. METHODS: A retrospective international multicenter cohort study was conducted across 11 centers (10 in Europe and one in India). Adult patients undergoing reconstruction with BMF after oncologic resection and a minimum follow-up of 6 months were included. Donor-site morbidity was assessed during dedicated follow-up visits using a standardized clinical scoring system evaluating mouth opening, oral commissure symmetry, vestibular restoration, cheek lining reconstruction, and cosmetic outcome. RESULTS: A total of 340 patients were included (mean age 58.6 ± 13.9 years; 50% female; mean flap area 14.6 ± 6.2 cm2). The mean donor-site outcome score was 10.7 ± 3.4. At multivariable linear mixed-effects analysis accounting for center, adjuvant radiotherapy or radiochemotherapy and donor-site closure by secondary healing were independently associated with lower scores, whereas the buccal artery myomucosal island flap and the tunnelized facial artery myomucosal island flap were associated with higher scores. Wound dehiscence was the most frequent complication (9.1%). In 223 patients with available data, higher adherence to rehabilitation exercises was associated with improved outcome scores, both with and without adjuvant radiotherapy. CONCLUSIONS: BMF provides reliable reconstruction with generally favorable donor-site outcomes. Morbidity is mainly influenced by adjuvant radiotherapy, donor-site management, flap design, and adherence to postoperative rehabilitation exercises.

item.title: The Utility of Artificial Intelligence for Conducting Systematic Reviews in Otolaryngology.
item.dc:creator: Shah KV, Rich DJ, Merlino D, Brody RM
item.description:
Authors: Shah KV, Rich DJ, Merlino D, Brody RM
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71037
Published: 2026-Nov-14
PMID: 43033058



Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The exponential growth in medical literature has strained traditional evidence synthesis approaches, prompting interest in artificial intelligence (AI) as a potential solution. Thus, we sought to assess the concordance and time savings between humans and AI in the systematic review process for a specialized otolaryngology topic. METHODS: A mock systematic review on immunotherapy for HPV+ oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma was conducted. Title/abstract and full-text were independently performed by human reviewers using Covidence and by Claude by Anthropic, model Sonnet 3.7. Concordance at each phase was assessed with sensitivity and specificity, and total time expenditure was documented for both approaches. Claude Sonnet 4.5 was subsequently applied to full-text screening of a published systematic review as proof-of-concept validation. RESULTS: Of the 1337 abstracts screened, human reviewers identified 43 for full-text review and ultimately included 17 manuscripts. Claude demonstrated an overall sensitivity of 17.6% (3/17) and specificity of 96.3% (1271/1320) when performing independent screening of all abstracts. When provided human-curated abstracts for full-text screening in an "AI-assisted" methodology, it achieved 100% (17/17) sensitivity and 57.7% (15/26) specificity. Validation against a published review achieved 100% sensitivity and 97.8% specificity. AI-driven screening required 325 active human minutes versus 1340 m for traditional human review, representing a theoretical active human time savings of over 75%. CONCLUSION: While AI cannot yet replace human judgment in systematic reviews, hybrid methodologies combining AI speed with human clinical expertise may represent the most promising approach for maintaining both efficiency and quality in evidence synthesis for rapidly evolving medical fields. Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nivolumab is an immune checkpoint inhibitor used for recurrent/metastatic squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) of the oral cavity, pharynx, and larynx; yet Australian real-world evidence remains limited. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using linked Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme dispensing and National Death Index mortality data for patients initiating nivolumab monotherapy during 2019-2023. item.title: Vascular and Circulating Blood Exposure to Proton or Photon Irradiation: Differentials in Lymphocyte Subset Metrics in Cancer Patients.
item.dc:creator: Meiriño R, Calvo FA, Amaya E, Burguete J, Serrano J, García Cardosa M, Pedrero D, Azcona D, Palma J, Fortuño MA, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Meiriño R, Calvo FA, Amaya E, Burguete J, Serrano J, García Cardosa M, Pedrero D, Azcona D, Palma J, Fortuño MA, et al.
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18213587
Published: 2026-Nov-08
PMID: 43026908



Abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Radiation-induced lymphopenia is consistently associated with adverse outcomes across solid tumours, yet the vascular compartment that carries the irradiated lymphocyte pool is not routinely delineated during treatment planning. The VASA project makes blood vessels an explicit, measurable structure in that process. Phase II aimed primarily to establish the feasibility of that delineation and secondarily to explore how dose-volume metrics computed on MRI-segmented vessels relate to serial immunophenotyping in patients treated with protons or photons. METHODS: Thirty-nine patients treated between March 2021 and May 2022 were studied prospectively (30 proton, 9 photon). Flow-contrast three-dimensional MRI with three velocity-encoding directions was added to simulation; vessel masks segmented semi-automatically from the sum-of-magnitude reconstruction were imported into the treatment-planning system to generate dose-volume histograms. The effective dose to circulating immune cells (EDIC), the integral dose to vessels (IDVe) and the integral dose to target were computed. Blood was sampled at the start and at the end of irradiation for lymphocyte counts and B, T and NK immunophenotyping. Groups were compared with Welch's t-test for continuous variables and Fisher's exact test for categorical variables, without correction for multiple comparisons; the photon subgroup was not matched. RESULTS: EDIC was higher with photons than protons (5.60 vs. 1.25 Gy; p = 0.005) and in patients who became lymphopenic (4.84 vs. 1.47 Gy; p = 0.027); IDVe differed in the same direction without reaching significance (3.60 vs. 0.53 Gy·L, p = 0.091; 3.08 vs. 0.67 Gy·L, p = 0.180). Within the proton cohort, EDIC and IDVe increased from brain to head-and-neck to thorax-abdomen targets (0.81, 1.11 and 2.17 Gy; 0.13, 0.26 and 1.63 Gy·L), and the IDVe ordering persisted after adjustment for target volume (p < 0.001). Lymphocyte counts fell from 1.92 to 1.43 × 103/µL in the proton cohort (p < 0.001), with the lowest end-of-treatment values in thorax-abdomen targets (1.31 × 103/µL). B, T and NK subpopulations all declined in the proton cohort; among regions, only head-and-neck targets showed significant T and NK losses. CONCLUSIONS: Patient-specific vascular delineation and dosimetry are feasible in a clinical planning workflow, and the resulting metrics track irradiation modality and the magnitude of lymphocyte depletion. These associations are exploratory; immune-sparing plan optimisation using vascular constraints remains a future application requiring prospective validation.

item.title: Metabolomics in Thoracic Oncology from Biomarker Discovery to Therapeutic Targeting: A Narrative Review.
item.dc:creator: Mahmoud MA, Sharma G, Sarkaria IS, Porembka MR, DeBerardinis RJ, Kernstine KH
item.description:
Authors: Mahmoud MA, Sharma G, Sarkaria IS, Porembka MR, DeBerardinis RJ, Kernstine KH
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18213582
Published: 2026-Nov-07
PMID: 43026902



Abstract:
Thoracic malignancies show context-dependent metabolic plasticity that influences growth, immune evasion, and treatment response. This review examines how metabolomics, stable-isotope tracing, and metabolic flux analysis complement molecular profiling in lung, esophageal, pleural, and thymic cancers. We distinguish metabolite abundance from isotope enrichment and quantitative flux, and review analytical platforms, computational workflows, histology-specific programs, immunometabolism, biomarkers, and therapy. Lung squamous cell carcinoma often depends on glycolysis, lung adenocarcinoma shows substrate and spatial heterogeneity, and molecular subsets of small cell lung cancer have preclinical vulnerabilities in arginine metabolism and guanosine nucleotide synthesis. Hypoxia and metabolite exchange among malignant, stromal, and immune cells may shape therapeutic resistance. Biofluid and tissue studies support early detection and monitoring, but most circulating signatures and findings in rare thoracic tumors remain exploratory. Translation is limited by confounding, incomplete metabolite identification, small cohorts, and limited external validation. Trials of unselected metabolic inhibitors have largely failed. Two biomarker-selected strategies have advanced: arginine deprivation in non-epithelioid pleural mesothelioma, a population enriched for argininosuccinate synthetase 1 (ASS1) deficiency, and PRMT5 inhibition in tumors with MTAP deletion. These results suggest that success may depend on selecting patients by a demonstrated metabolic dependency rather than by the plausibility of the target. Progress requires harmonized multicenter workflows, paired tissue and biofluid sampling, rigorous validation, and integration with spatial, single-cell, multi-omic, and clinical data.

item.title: Prospective comparison of CT- and MRI-based tumor delineation based on intraoperative navigation and spatially annotated pathology in locally advanced midfacial squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Bauer L, Kühle R, Fuchs J, Moratin J, Deng M, Ehle M, Schindehütte R, Schröter P, Stritzke F, Kozyra K, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Bauer L, Kühle R, Fuchs J, Moratin J, Deng M, Ehle M, Schindehütte R, Schröter P, Stritzke F, Kozyra K, et al.
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1884392
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43065419



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Precise tumor delineation is critical for navigation-guided surgery and radiotherapy (RT) in locally advanced midfacial squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are both recommended for staging and provide complementary information. However, quantitative comparisons of CT- and MRI-based tumor contours remain scarce, while a spatial comparison with histopathological data has never been performed. Therefore, we prospectively compared gross tumor volumes (GTV) derived from CT and MRI before navigation-guided surgery and correlated the results with spatially annotated pathology. METHODS: This imaging sub-analysis was conducted within the prospective NAVIGATORR trial (NCT05671458). Fifteen patients with locally advanced midfacial SCC underwent contrast-enhanced CT and 1.5T or 3T MRI (T1w, T2w, DWI) for navigation-based surgery planning. Datasets were rigidly co-registered and an experienced radiologist independently contoured the GTV on CT and MRI while blinded to the other modality. Besides qualitative and volumetric evaluation, spatial agreement was assessed using the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and Hausdorff distance (HD). Tumor contours were correlated with spatially annotated intraoperative biopsy locations and histopathological results. RESULTS: Fifteen patients and 109 spatially annotated biopsy locations (19 tumor-positive) were analyzed. MRI was preferred for tumor delineation by the radiologist in all cases, with superior differentiation between tumor and mucosal swelling (73%) and improved soft tissue contrast (67%). MRI based GTVs were significantly larger than CT-based GTVs (median 28.3 ml vs. 16.8 ml; p = 0.02). DSC values demonstrated fair agreement with considerable heterogeneity (median 0.58; IQR 0.47-0.65), and median HD was 16 mm (IQR 12-27 mm). MRI-based contours encompassed numerically more tumor-positive biopsy locations than CT-based contours (6/19 vs. 1/19; clustered McNemar p = 0.20) while including fewer tumor-negative locations (7/90 vs. 10/90; p = 0.53). At patient level, at least one tumor-positive biopsy was located inside the contour in 3/8 (MRI) vs. 1/8 (CT) patients. DISCUSSION: GTV delineation differs substantially between MRI and CT in locally advanced midfacial SCC, and the two modalities provide complementary information. These exploratory findings support the complementary use of MRI and CT for tumor visualization. Clinical implications remain to be shown by the primary endpoint analysis of the NAVIGATORR trial.

item.title: Perioperative and Long-Term Outcomes of Surgery in Patients Aged 80 Years or Older with Esophageal or Esophagogastric Junction Cancer: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis.
item.dc:creator: Ochiai T, Nakajima M, Nakagawa M, Fujita J, Mise M, Maeda Y, Yoshimatsu M, Amagai E, Morita S, Kojima K
item.description:
Authors: Ochiai T, Nakajima M, Nakagawa M, Fujita J, Mise M, Maeda Y, Yoshimatsu M, Amagai E, Morita S, Kojima K
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18213574
Published: 2026-Nov-06
PMID: 43026894



Abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: With population aging, determining appropriate surgical indications for patients aged ≥80 years with esophageal or esophagogastric junction cancer has become increasingly important. This study compared perioperative and long-term outcomes between surgically treated patients aged ≥80 years and those aged <80 years. METHODS: Patients who underwent surgery for esophageal or esophagogastric junction cancer between April 2009 and April 2026 were retrospectively analyzed. Propensity score matching was performed using sex, American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status, tumor location, histological type, clinical stage, surgical procedure, and neoadjuvant chemotherapy. After matching, 40 patients were included in each group. Perioperative outcomes, postoperative complications, overall survival (OS), and disease-specific survival (DSS) were compared. RESULTS: Operative time, blood loss, and postoperative hospital stay did not differ significantly between the groups. Patients aged ≥80 years had fewer dissected lymph nodes (26.0 vs. 48.5, p = 0.003) and a lower incidence of Clavien-Dindo grade ≥IIIa complications (17.5% vs. 40.0%, p = 0.047). The incidences of pneumonia, recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy, and anastomotic leakage did not differ significantly. The 5-year OS was lower in patients aged ≥80 years (32.9% vs. 55.3%, p = 0.006; HR, 2.31; 95% CI, 1.24-4.28), whereas 5-year DSS did not differ significantly (55.4% vs. 69.0%, p = 0.122; HR, 1.86; 95% CI, 0.84-4.12). CONCLUSIONS: Surgery may be feasible in carefully selected patients aged ≥80 years. These findings do not establish a survival advantage over non-surgical treatment. Surgical eligibility should be based on overall condition, oncological factors, and anticipated surgical invasiveness rather than chronological age alone.

item.title: Health Disparities in Management of Keratinocyte Carcinoma: A Multicenter Observational Study.
item.dc:creator: Debaveye M, Destrooper L, Waalboer-Spuij R, Meertens A, Hoorens I
item.description:
Authors: Debaveye M, Destrooper L, Waalboer-Spuij R, Meertens A, Hoorens I
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18213561
Published: 2026-Nov-06
PMID: 43026881



Abstract:
Background/Objectives: Keratinocyte carcinoma (KC) treatment is guided primarily by tumor characteristics, but sociodemographic factors may also influence care. We examined associations of age, sex, marital status, and educational level with treatment selection. Methods: Adults with actinic keratosis or KC were recruited in four Belgian and Dutch settings between 2020 and September 2023. Treatment was categorized as topical/non-invasive therapy, Mohs micrographic surgery (MMS), or standard surgical excision (reference). Multinomial regression adjusted for histologic group, tumor size, location, recruiting center, and an age-independent Charlson comorbidity component. The primary analysis included 681 participants, with additional sensitivity analyses. Results: The model converged normally. Age (global p = 0.023) and educational level (p = 0.002) were associated with treatment selection; sex and marital status were not. Each additional decade of age was associated with lower odds of MMS versus standard excision (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.755, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.595-0.959). Low versus high education was associated with lower odds of topical/non-invasive treatment versus standard excision (aOR 0.123, 95% CI 0.034-0.450), but not with MMS (aOR 0.533, 95% CI 0.232-1.222). Conclusions: Age and educational level were associated with KC treatment selection after clinical and center adjustment. These associations do not establish inequitable care because relevant patient-, clinician-, and pathway-level determinants were not captured.

item.title: From ancient remedy to modern use: cannabis and cannabinoids in cancer care in the United States.
item.dc:creator: Behl D, Abrams DI, Zylla DM, D'Andre SD
item.description:
Authors: Behl D, Abrams DI, Zylla DM, D'Andre SD
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1878313
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43061359



Abstract:
Cannabis, an ancient plant that has been used for millennia, is increasingly utilized by patients with cancer to alleviate symptoms related to both the disease and its treatment. This complex botanical contains multiple bioactive compounds, most notably delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) and cannabidiol (CBD), which interact with the endogenous endocannabinoid system. THC has been studied the most, and synthetic cannabinoids are approved for the management of chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting. However, evidence supporting cannabis for other cancer-related symptoms-including chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy, insomnia, appetite stimulation, and non-neuropathic pain-remains limited. CBD alone has not demonstrated consistent or meaningful clinical benefit. Although preclinical data exist, there is no clinical evidence supporting cannabis as a cancer treatment. Cannabis may interact with prescribed medications, particularly with high-dose oral formulations, and its effects on immunotherapy are under investigation. Overall, cannabis is generally well tolerated, though adverse effects can be significant. Use is discouraged in individuals under 25 years of age due to ongoing neurodevelopment, and patients with active psychiatric or cardiovascular conditions should use cannabis only under close clinical supervision.

item.title: Association between postoperative glutamine supplementation and short-term outcomes after ileostomy reversal in patients with colorectal cancer: a retrospective cohort study.
item.dc:creator: Xiao D, Zhou X, Li Q, Xie J
item.description:
Authors: Xiao D, Zhou X, Li Q, Xie J
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1950443
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43060455



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Ileostomy reversal is associated with substantial postoperative morbidity despite being considered a relatively minor surgical procedure. Although glutamine supplementation has been investigated in gastrointestinal surgery, evidence regarding its role in patients undergoing ileostomy reversal remains limited. This study evaluated the association between postoperative glutamine supplementation and short-term outcomes following ileostomy reversal in patients with colorectal cancer. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients with colorectal cancer who underwent elective ileostomy reversal between January 2015 and December 2025. Patients were classified into the glutamine group, who received postoperative intravenous glutamine supplementation, and the control group. Postoperative outcomes within 30 days, including complications, gastrointestinal recovery, and length of hospital stay, were compared between groups. RESULTS: A total of 183 patients were included, comprising 103 patients in the glutamine group and 80 in the control group. After 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM), 74 matched pairs were identified. Compared with the control group, the glutamine group had a significantly lower incidence of overall postoperative complications (14.9% vs. 29.7%, P = 0.043) and infectious complications (9.5% vs. 23.0%, P = 0.041). The glutamine group also had shorter times to first flatus, first defecation, and initiation of oral diets, as well as lower incidences of postoperative nausea and vomiting and abdominal distension. Hospital stay was shorter in the glutamine group. No significant between-group differences were observed in postoperative serum prealbumin, total protein, or albumin levels. CONCLUSIONS: In this PSM study, postoperative glutamine supplementation was associated with fewer postoperative complications, faster gastrointestinal recovery, and shorter hospital stay following ileostomy reversal in patients with colorectal cancer. These findings indicate a potential association between glutamine supplementation and favorable short-term postoperative outcomes and warrant confirmation in prospective randomized studies.

item.title: Salivary glands auto-segmentation in head and neck radiotherapy: imaging modalities, models, and clinical relevance.
item.dc:creator: Wong WL, Shum CY, Chow YL, Man KH, Law HKW, Tam SY
item.description:
Authors: Wong WL, Shum CY, Chow YL, Man KH, Law HKW, Tam SY
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1923659
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43054526



Abstract:
Radiotherapy-induced salivary gland injury is a major contributor to xerostomia and impaired quality of life in patients with head and neck cancer, making accurate organ-at-risk delineation clinically important. Deep learning-based auto-segmentation has the potential to improve contouring efficiency and consistency, but reported performance is heterogeneous and its clinical significance is not always clear. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on salivary gland auto-segmentation across computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and prostate-specific membrane antigen positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PSMA PET-CT), with particular emphasis on gland-specific challenges, performance evaluation, and clinical translation. CT has the largest evidence base and remains most relevant to routine radiotherapy planning, whereas MRI provides improved soft-tissue visualization and PSMA PET-CT offers high functional contrast for selected salivary structures. Across modalities, segmentation performance is generally more challenging for smaller structures, particularly the sublingual and tubarial gland regions. Importantly, geometric metrics such as the Dice similarity coefficient do not alone establish clinical acceptability or dosimetric equivalence; evaluation should also consider boundary accuracy, expert correction burden, clinical acceptability, and dosimetric impact. Current evidence is further limited by heterogeneous study designs and reference standards, scarce external validation, and limited evidence linking auto-segmentation directly to treatment-related toxicity or patient outcomes. Future research should prioritize multi-institutional validation, clinically meaningful evaluation, improved segmentation of small glands, and human-in-the-loop integration into adaptive radiotherapy. Overall, auto-segmentation represents a promising tool for salivary gland delineation, but its clinical implementation should be supported by evidence extending beyond geometric accuracy alone.

item.title: Radiomics-driven multimodal integration in precision radiotherapy for nasopharyngeal carcinoma- current evidence, clinical barriers, and future directions.
item.dc:creator: Ma Y, Xie Y, Gou Q, Chen N, Gou Q
item.description:
Authors: Ma Y, Xie Y, Gou Q, Chen N, Gou Q
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1902266
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43054349



Abstract:
Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), a head and neck malignancy, is highly sensitive to radiation. Accordingly, radiotherapy has long been the primary curative modality for patients with non-metastatic NPC. Although intensity-modulated radiotherapy has significantly improved target conformality and normal tissue protection, local recurrence, distant metastasis, and late toxicity remain important issues in long-term management. To achieve a balance between tumor control and normal tissue protection, the continuous integration of multi-source information throughout the treatment workflow is critical. Radiomics has the potential to quantify spatial heterogeneity that may not be fully captured by conventional visual assessment. In this review, radiomics-driven multimodal integration refers to the task-specific combination of imaging-derived phenotypes with complementary clinical variables, Epstein-Barr virus DNA (EBV-DNA), hematological biomarkers, dose distributions, pathological features, molecular data, longitudinal imaging, or treatment-delivery information for defined radiotherapy decisions. This review focuses on the clinical timeline of precision radiotherapy for NPC and provides an overview of radiomics-driven multimodal integration studies. It discusses the current applications and limitations of this framework in pretreatment risk stratification and treatment selection, target volume and organ-at-risk definition during radiotherapy planning, on-treatment monitoring and adaptive radiotherapy, toxicity prediction and normal-tissue protection, and post-treatment recurrence assessment and re-irradiation decision-making. This synthesis of current evidence, clinical barriers, and methodological considerations may inform future validation and implementation of radiomics-driven multimodal integration in NPC precision radiotherapy.

item.title: Proton beam therapy in the treatment of adenoid cystic carcinoma of the head and neck: a single enterprise retrospective cohort study.
item.dc:creator: Rohit A, Voss M, Gunn H, Ma D, Patel S, Lester S, Rwigema JC, Neben-Wittich M, Foote R, Routman DM, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Rohit A, Voss M, Gunn H, Ma D, Patel S, Lester S, Rwigema JC, Neben-Wittich M, Foote R, Routman DM, et al.
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1968350
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43054136



Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) is a rare salivary gland malignancy with high propensity for perineural invasion (PNI) and relative radioresistance. Proton beam therapy (PBT) may improve tumor control through improved target coverage, as well as higher physical and biologic dose while limiting dose to surrounding critical structures. This single-enterprise two-site study reports outcomes and toxicity in patients with ACC of the head and neck (HN) region treated with curative-intent PBT. METHODS: From 2015-2025, 89 patients with HN ACC were treated with curative-intent PBT. Patients with distant metastases or prior radiotherapy (RT) were excluded. Clinical outcomes were assessed retrospectively. Toxicities were recorded prospectively using CTCAE v5.0. The Kaplan-Meier method was used to estimate local tumor control (LC), distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS) and overall survival (OS). Hazard ratios, 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and test of association between tumor and treatment variables and outcomes were estimated using Cox proportional hazards regression analysis. RESULTS: Median follow-up was 3.1 years. Sixty-nine patients underwent surgery followed by postoperative PBT, while 20 received definitive PBT for unresectable disease. The 3-year LC rate was 98.3% following postoperative PBT and 82.6% following definitive PBT. Treatment approach was not significantly associated with LC. Three-year DMFS was 86.2% and 64.9%, respectively, while 3-year OS was 94.4% in both cohorts. Twenty-one patients developed distant metastases, most commonly involving the lungs. Six patients experienced acute grade 3 toxicities, including dysphagia, mucositis, and dermatitis; seven experienced late grade 3 toxicities, most commonly osteoradionecrosis (n=4). One patient had both acute and late toxicity. No grade 4 or 5 toxicities occurred. CONCLUSIONS: Curative-intent PBT was associated with favorable LC and acceptable toxicity. Outcomes according to definitive versus postoperative treatment should be interpreted descriptively due to substantial baseline differences between groups and confounding by indication. Longer follow-up and larger studies are needed.

item.title: Pretreatment platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio and survival after definitive radio(chemo)therapy for head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: an exploratory cohort study.
item.dc:creator: Werner J, Lehnick D, Strobel K, Stenz NA, Morand GB, Rajan GP
item.description:
Authors: Werner J, Lehnick D, Strobel K, Stenz NA, Morand GB, Rajan GP
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1970136
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43054093



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Current staging provides limited prognostic accuracy in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). We evaluated whether pretreatment systemic inflammatory ratios and 2-deoxy-2-[18F]fluoro-D-glucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography ([18F]FDG PET/CT) metabolic parameters are associated with survival in patients treated with definitive radio(chemo)therapy. METHODS: We retrospectively studied 110 patients with HNSCC treated with definitive radio(chemo)therapy at a single center. Inflammatory ratios, including the platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), were derived from a pretreatment blood count. Metabolic parameters were obtained from staging [18F]FDG PET/CT. The primary endpoints were overall survival (OS) and disease-specific survival (DSS). A Cox model comprising PLR, p16 status, cT category and age was fitted for each endpoint. Missing p16 status was handled by multiple imputation. RESULTS: A higher PLR was independently associated with worse OS (HR per interquartile range 1.61, 95% CI 1.13-2.28; p = 0.008) and DSS (HR 1.78, 95% CI 1.21-2.60; p = 0.003), alongside p16-negativity. cT4 category and age were also independently associated with OS. p16 was missing in 30% of patients, mostly non-oropharyngeal tumors. Complete-case analysis was therefore restricted to 77 patients, in which the point estimates were similar, but the association no longer reached significance. PLR correlated weakly with cT category (Spearman ρ = 0.275, p = 0.004) without collinearity. In exploratory analyses, the association between a high PLR and worse survival was clear in oropharyngeal tumors but weaker in other subsites. Metabolic parameters did not demonstrate an independent association with survival after adjustment. CONCLUSIONS: Pretreatment PLR was independently associated with worse OS and DSS in HNSCC treated with definitive radio(chemo)therapy in the primary multiple-imputation analysis. Effect estimates were consistent in direction and magnitude across all three approaches to missing p16 status. A higher PLR indicates a worse prognosis, but the association is modest and does not guide treatment selection. Prospective validation with prespecified cutoffs is required before clinical use.

item.title: Differences in variant profile between follicular thyroid carcinoma and adenoma: targeted next-generation sequencing study.
item.dc:creator: Lai CC, Chang TA, Chen YJ
item.description:
Authors: Lai CC, Chang TA, Chen YJ
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1902761
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43053988



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Preoperative ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration cytology cannot reliably distinguish follicular thyroid carcinoma (FTC) from follicular thyroid adenoma (FTA), making these neoplasms particularly challenging to diagnose. Although several studies have explored variant differences using targeted next-generation sequencing (NGS) panels, the molecular distinctions between FTC and FTA remain incompletely defined. In this study, targeted NGS was performed on DNA from 52 formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded specimens. METHODS: Genomic DNA was extracted, quality assessed, and targeted NGS performed for 14 genes commonly mutated in thyroid neoplasms. Synonymous variants were excluded, and analyses then focused on pathogenic alterations. Variant frequencies were evaluated at both the locus and gene levels in FTC and FTA. RESULTS: After excluding synonymous variants, 1,074 variants across 14 genes were identified, with 92.8% clustered in five genes: TERT (70.5%), TSHR (8.6%), RET (5.9%), TP53 (4.2%), and BRAF (3.6%). FTC and FTA exhibited distinct variant landscapes, and TERT variants were significantly enriched in FTC. EIF1AX splice site variants (chrX:20148727; c.338-2A>C and c.338-2A>T) were significantly associated with FTC. In the pathogenic dataset, each additional EIF1AX variant increased the likelihood of FTC by 15.4-fold. In contrast, RET and PTEN variants were more frequent in FTA, and each additional RET variant reduced the probability of FTC by nearly half (odds ratio, 0.489). CONCLUSION: These findings underscored the potential diagnostic utility of variant profiling. TERT and EIF1AX variants were predictors of malignant transformation, whereas RET and PTEN variants were more frequently detected in FTA. Their diagnostic and therapeutic utility warrants further validation in clinical settings.

item.title: Transcript Abundance of IL6, CXCL9, LIF and LIFR in Glottic Lesions: Relationship to Histology and to Narrow-Band Imaging Vascular Patterns.
item.dc:creator: Barańska M, Borkowska E, Pietruszewska W
item.description:
Authors: Barańska M, Borkowska E, Pietruszewska W
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18213545
Published: 2026-Nov-04
PMID: 43026866



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Narrow-band imaging (NBI) is an established adjunct in laryngeal lesion assessment, but the molecular processes underlying high-risk vascular patterns are poorly defined. We compared IL6, CXCL9, LIF, and LIFR transcript abundance between glottic carcinoma and non-cancerous lesions, related it to NBI patterns, and tested whether IL6 adds diagnostic information to NBI. METHODS: In this prospective single-center exploratory study, 62 patients operated on for glottic lesions (33 squamous cell carcinomas, 29 non-cancerous lesions) underwent preoperative NBI (European Laryngological Society and Ni classifications); transcripts were quantified by RT-qPCR. RESULTS: IL6 was higher in carcinoma (median 5.97 vs. 0.30; p = 0.004), also with non-detects set to the detection limit (p = 0.001) and among ever-smokers only (p = 0.0008). Sex adjustment attenuated the association (OR 1.78 per 10-fold increase, 95% CI 0.98-3.23; p = 0.06); smoking could not be adjusted for, as all carcinomas occurred in ever-smokers. CXCL9, LIF, and LIFR did not differ. Adding IL6 to NBI did not improve discrimination (ΔAUC 0.00-0.02; bootstrap 95% CIs including zero). Within non-cancerous lesions, IL6 was nominally higher in high-risk NBI patterns (n = 5-7), but no stratified comparison survived false-discovery-rate correction. CONCLUSIONS: IL6 transcript abundance was higher in glottic carcinoma, but the difference was sensitive to sex adjustment and, when measured in bulk tissue, may reflect lesion composition, including inflammatory infiltrate. IL6 showed no evidence of diagnostic value beyond NBI, and its link with vascular morphology remains a hypothesis.

item.title: Real-World Outcomes of Oral VEGFR Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor-Containing Therapy in Unresectable Malignant Mesothelioma: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
item.dc:creator: Liu Z, Zhong J, Wan R, Duan JC, Wang ZJ, Bai H, Wang J
item.description:
Authors: Liu Z, Zhong J, Wan R, Duan JC, Wang ZJ, Bai H, Wang J
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18213541
Published: 2026-Nov-04
PMID: 43026862



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Systemic treatment choices after failure of standard therapy are limited for malignant mesothelioma. Oral vascular endothelial growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors (VEGFR-TKIs) have been incorporated into salvage treatment strategies, but real-world evidence regarding their effectiveness and safety remains scarce. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed a single-center cohort comprising patients with pathologically confirmed malignant mesothelioma treated at Cancer Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences/National Cancer Center between 1 April 2017 and 16 March 2023. Patients with unresectable disease who received a VEGFR-TKI-containing regimen and had sufficient clinical follow-up for outcome assessment were included. Progression-free survival (PFS) served as the primary endpoint. Objective response rate (ORR), disease control rate (DCR), overall survival (OS) from VEGFR-TKI initiation, and recorded adverse events were included as secondary endpoints. RESULTS: The cohort comprised 48 patients, with a median follow-up of 24.0 months. The Kaplan-Meier estimated median PFS was 4.8 months (95% CI, 2.9-8.8), and median OS from VEGFR-TKI initiation was 17.9 months (95% CI, 13.5-not estimable). Among 39 response-evaluable patients, 6 achieved partial response, 20 had stable disease, and 13 had progressive disease as their best overall response, yielding an ORR of 15.4% and a DCR of 66.7%. Two patients remained progression-free for more than 24 months. Grade 3 adverse events in the records included hematuria, hypertension, and nausea/vomiting; no grade 4 or grade 5 adverse event was documented. CONCLUSIONS: VEGFR-TKI-containing therapy was associated with clinically relevant disease control in unresectable malignant mesothelioma, with durable benefit observed in a small subset of patients. These observations warrant further evaluation of VEGFR-TKI-based salvage strategies in larger multicenter cohorts.

item.title: A systematic review: is contralateral elective neck dissection or neck radiotherapy indicated in lateralised cT3/T4 N0 oral squamous cell carcinoma?
item.dc:creator: Obialo N, Tagdiwala PA, Cassidy O, Schilling C, Eldweny H, Leung B, Bisase B, Norris P, Doumas SN
item.description:
Authors: Obialo N, Tagdiwala PA, Cassidy O, Schilling C, Eldweny H, Leung B, Bisase B, Norris P, Doumas SN
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1944716
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43047546



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Contralateral cervical lymph node metastasis remains a therapeutic challenge in patients with lateralised T3/T4 N0 oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), with current guidelines offering differing recommendations regarding management of the contralateral neck. METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA. MEDLINE and Embase were searched from January 2008 to March 2026 for studies evaluating contralateral neck management in lateralised T3/T4 N0 OSCC. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I and QUADAS-2, according to study design. Where possible, a meta-analysis was undertaken by combining outcome measures, otherwise due to anticipated heterogeneity a narrative synthesis was used. RESULTS: Search of the databases revealed 10,670 articles, following deduplication 5,173 were screened and 23 articles were sought for retrieval. Thirteen studies were included, involving 2,764 patients, predominantly retrospective cohorts; 561 were clearly identified as well lateralised T3N0 or T4N0. The tongue was the most common tumour subsite. A random-effects meta-analysis of proportions demonstrated a pooled contralateral neck disease rate of 16.1% (95% CI 1.2-51.7%), the 95% prediction interval was 0.1-90.3%, indicating substantial between-study heterogeneity (I² = 93.5%). Available studies did not provide sufficient evidence to determine whether elective contralateral neck treatment improves locoregional control, disease-free survival or cancer specific survival compared with observation. Interpretation was limited by retrospective study designs, heterogeneity and potential confounding. Sentinel lymph node biopsy and lymphoscintigraphy-guided approaches may help identify selected patients at risk of contralateral disease, although evidence in advanced tumours remains limited. DISCUSSION: Overall, the current evidence is insufficient to support or oppose routine elective contralateral neck dissection or radiotherapy in lateralised T3/T4 N0 OSCC. Selective lymphatic mapping may support more individualised management, but prospective validation is required before its routine use. item.title: Comparative effectiveness of five treatment strategies for locally advanced oral squamous cell carcinoma in resource-limited settings: a multinomial overlap-weighted real-world cohort study.
item.dc:creator: Song L, Chen Y, Pan Z, Ma Z, Li J, Jiang L
item.description:
Authors: Song L, Chen Y, Pan Z, Ma Z, Li J, Jiang L
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1993812
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43047457



Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: For locally advanced oral squamous cell carcinoma (LA-OSCC), radical surgery followed by risk-adapted postoperative radiotherapy or concurrent chemoradiotherapy is standard. In resource-limited settings, limited radiotherapy access, costs, and poor tolerance yield multiple pragmatic strategies. Prior real-world studies mostly used pairwise comparisons, lacking systematic evaluation of all coexisting strategies within one framework. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 388 patients with LA-OSCC treated between January 2019 and December 2022, classified into five groups by actual treatment received: surgery with adjuvant chemoradiotherapy (surgery plus CRT), surgery with adjuvant radiotherapy (surgery plus RT), surgery with adjuvant chemotherapy (surgery plus CT), surgery alone, and definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT). Multinomial overlap weighting targeting the average treatment effect in the overlap population (OW-ATO) balanced 10 baseline covariates, and overlap-weighted Cox models with robust variance estimation compared overall survival (OS), disease-free survival (DFS), and disease-specific survival (DSS). Two-group (surgery versus definitive CRT) and four-group (operated patients, pathology-adjusted) analyses, competing-risk models, and sensitivity analyses (IPTW-ATE, landmark, early-death exclusion, E-value, bootstrap) assessed robustness. RESULTS: After overlap weighting, the maximum absolute pairwise standardized mean difference decreased from 0.548 to 0.168. Compared with surgery plus CRT, surgery plus RT showed no statistically significant differences in OS (hazard ratio [HR] 1.33, 95% CI 0.76-2.33), DFS (HR 1.23, 95% CI 0.79-1.90), or DSS (HR 1.56, 95% CI 0.77-3.15), whereas surgery plus CT (OS HR 2.54, 95% CI 1.47-4.39), surgery alone (OS HR 3.21, 95% CI 1.94-5.32), and definitive CRT (OS HR 3.31, 95% CI 1.97-5.57) were each associated with significantly worse outcomes across all three endpoints. Findings were consistent across all analytical layers and sensitivity analyses. CONCLUSIONS: In resource-limited real-world settings, surgery-based multimodal strategies were associated with better survival in LA-OSCC. Surgery plus RT did not differ significantly from surgery plus CRT; however, given wide confidence intervals and limited power, equivalence was not established, and it should be considered only a potential de-escalation option for selected patients who cannot receive concurrent chemotherapy-not as a replacement for standard chemoradiotherapy in high-risk disease. Surgery plus CT should be reserved as a second-best option when radiotherapy is completely unavailable.

item.title: Single-cell and spatially resolved immune profiling in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: a bibliometric and thematic analysis.
item.dc:creator: Li Y, Wang B, Zhang N, Peng G
item.description:
Authors: Li Y, Wang B, Zhang N, Peng G
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1985265
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43047303



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Single-cell and spatially resolved technologies have expanded research on immune heterogeneity in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). We examined relationships among research themes, their cited foundations, and their temporal representation. METHODS: Web of Science Core Collection and PubMed were searched for publications dated from 1900 through July 1, 2026. After deduplication and screening, 587 English-language articles and reviews were included. Bibliometric networks were analyzed using VOSviewer, R, and bibliometrix. Document-level cosine overlaps between keyword and reference clusters were evaluated using stratified permutations with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment. Temporal analyses used keyword proportions and citation-weighted reference-year profiles within three descriptive windows. Sensitivity analyses examined database composition, inclusion thresholds, and individual recent references. RESULTS: Publication output increased after 2021. China had the largest publication output, while the United States had the highest citation count and international-collaboration total link strength. Co-citation and keyword analyses identified four and three domains, respectively. K3-C2 had the largest observed cosine score (0.661), exceeding its null mean by 0.039 (adjusted P = 0.0072); K1-C1 also exceeded its null expectation (adjusted P = 0.0012). Among keyword-available publications, spatial transcriptomics increased from 0.0% to 1.7% and 8.3% across the three windows. The recent reference subset contained five references, all published in 2024; its C2 share was sensitive to individual references. Keyword-cluster agreement was high across database sources and moderate at the stricter occurrence threshold. CONCLUSION: The analysis identifies relationships among immune, cellular, stromal, spatial, and computational literature domains and descriptive changes in keyword representation. These findings provide a quantitative literature framework for further investigation of HNSCC immune profiling.

item.title: Targeted alpha therapy for solid tumors: biological rationale, clinical advances, and future perspectives.
item.dc:creator: Li Q, Xie J, Chen F, Li L, Yang C
item.description:
Authors: Li Q, Xie J, Chen F, Li L, Yang C
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.2007300
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43041765



Abstract:
Targeted alpha therapy (TAT) delivers high-linear-energy-transfer radiation over a few cell diameters and is being explored for resistant and microscopic solid-tumor disease. This targeted narrative review evaluates alpha-emitting platforms and clinical evidence by tumor type and development stage, with a focused literature update through 12 October 2026. Unlike broader radiochemistry-centered reviews, we place approved, randomized, early-phase, observational, and preclinical findings in separate evidence tiers. Radium-223 dichloride has randomized survival evidence in symptomatic bone-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, whereas molecularly targeted actinium-225, lead-212, astatine-211, and thorium-227 agents remain investigational in the indications discussed. Updated examples include the 2026 ACTION-1 actinium-225-DOTATATE dosimetry substudy, the 2026 first-in-human astatine-211-MABG study, 2025 lead-212-DOTAMTATE phase II disclosures, and a negative 2025 mesothelin-targeted thorium-227 study. Quantitative outcomes are reported with their study design and limitations rather than interpreted as indirect head-to-head comparisons. Major barriers include isotope supply, incomplete daughter retention, salivary, marrow, and kidney toxicity, spatially heterogeneous target uptake, and uncertainty in patient-specific microdosimetry. We propose practical, imaging-led selection and a priority-ranked translational roadmap.

item.title: Artificial intelligence in pediatric head and neck tumor imaging: a mini review of current applications and future directions.
item.dc:creator: Lotfian G, Ginat DT
item.description:
Authors: Lotfian G, Ginat DT
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.2010320
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43041688



Abstract:
Artificial intelligence (AI) is creating new opportunities to enhance medical imaging in pediatric oncology through quantitative image analysis and clinical decision support. This mini review examines the emerging role of AI in pediatric head and neck tumor imaging, including applications in lesion detection and characterization, tumor segmentation and volumetric analysis, treatment planning, longitudinal surveillance, prognostication, and precision medicine. Particular attention is given to the challenges of translating these approaches to pediatric populations, where rare and heterogeneous tumors, limited datasets, variable imaging protocols, and insufficient multicenter validation remain important barriers. We also discuss emerging strategies that may facilitate clinical translation, including federated learning, multimodal data integration, explainable AI, and integration with existing radiology workflows. Although pediatric-specific evidence remains limited, continued multicenter collaboration and prospective validation may enable AI-based tools to provide more reproducible quantitative imaging assessment and increasingly personalized clinical decision support. Ultimately, the clinical value of these technologies will depend on their ability to augment radiologist expertise and improve patient care through responsible integration into routine practice.

item.title: Long-term outcomes of globe-sparing surgery combined with adjuvant radiotherapy for lacrimal gland adenoid cystic carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Zhao SX, Xu WQ, Zhao XH, Su D, Li YY, Ma R, Hei Y, Mu XT, Yang XJ
item.description:
Authors: Zhao SX, Xu WQ, Zhao XH, Su D, Li YY, Ma R, Hei Y, Mu XT, Yang XJ
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1934640
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43041427



Abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate long-term outcomes of radiotherapy after globe-sparing surgery for lacrimal gland adenoid cystic carcinoma (LGACC) and compare different radiotherapy protocols. METHODS: This retrospective comparative case series included 97 patients with LGACC treated with globe-sparing surgery followed by postoperative radiotherapy between November 2003 and April 2023. Patients received one of four protocols differing in clinical target volume (CTV) expansion and radiation dose. Primary outcomes included locoregional recurrence, distant metastasis, locoregional recurrence-free survival (LRFS), distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS), progression-free survival, and overall survival. RESULTS: The median age was 38 years, and median follow-up was 7.2 years. The overall 5-, 10-, and 15-year LRFS rates were 80.2%, 74.5%, and 74.5%, respectively. Multivariable analysis identified R2 resection (HR = 4.16, 95% CI: 1.53‑11.35, P = 0.005), cribriform histology (HR = 0.26, 95% CI: 0.08‑0.81, P = 0.020), and smaller CTV expansion (≤0.5 cm; HR = 4.06, 95% CI: 1.41‑11.67, P = 0.009) as independent predictors of local recurrence. Patients treated with ≤0.5-cm CTV expansion and ≤54 Gy had significantly lower 5-, 10-, and 15-year LRFS rates (55.2%, 40.5%, and 40.5%) than those treated with 1-cm CTV expansion and 60-80 Gy (90.5%, 90.5%, and 90.5%; P < 0.001). DMFS did not differ significantly between groups (P = 0.599). Best-corrected visual acuity of 20/20-20/40 was preserved in 35.1% of patients. The 5-year risk of radiation retinopathy was 25.1% and 43.6% (P = 0.057) in the no extended-margin and extended-margin groups, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Radiotherapy with 1-cm CTV expansion and a dose of 60 Gy after globe-sparing surgery provided favorable locoregional control for LGACC. Distant metastasis remained the predominant cause of treatment failure.

item.title: TMSB10 marks a malignant epithelial programme spatially associated with fibroblast-matrix niches in oral squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Yao B, Tang Y, Liu S, Nie X, Lin L, Xu Q
item.description:
Authors: Yao B, Tang Y, Liu S, Nie X, Lin L, Xu Q
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1969309
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43041408



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Malignant epithelial states at the tumour-stroma interface may contribute to local invasion in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), but their reproducibility across patients and spatial relationship with fibroblast-matrix niches remain unclear. METHODS: Single-cell transcriptomes from 16 untreated OSCC samples were analysed to localise TMSB10 and derive a TMSB10-associated invasion-related programme (TIP) through within-patient comparisons of aneuploid epithelial cells. Frozen TIP scores were evaluated in independent single-cell and spatial cohorts. Spatial associations were tested using adjusted generalised additive models and random-effects meta-analysis. Survival associations were examined in GSE41613 and TCGA-HNSC, and TMSB10 was silenced in HN6 and HN30 cells. RESULTS: Among 89, 323 cells, TMSB10 was highly expressed in epithelial and endothelial compartments. TMSB10-high aneuploid epithelial cells exhibited 1, 569 differentially expressed genes and enrichment of 16 Hallmark pathways related to proliferation, oxidative metabolism, and epithelial plasticity. Frozen TIP scores showed concordant directions across patients and in GSE103322. TIP-core and TIP-anchor were positively associated with cancer-associated fibroblast/extracellular matrix (CAF/ECM) scores in all 18 spatial sections, with pooled effects of 0.1434 and 0.1456, respectively (both FDR = 0.000402); this association was reproduced in all four GSE220978 patients. In GSE41613, higher TMSB10 expression was associated with poorer overall and disease-specific survival after clinical adjustment, whereas TCGA-HNSC showed no consistent adjusted association. TMSB10 knockdown reduced CCK-8 signals, wound closure, and Transwell migration in both cell lines. CONCLUSION: Within malignant epithelial cells, TMSB10 expression is associated with a reproducible, pEMT-related programme spatially associated with CAF/ECM-rich regions. Knockdown findings support the involvement of TMSB10 in OSCC cell growth and migration.

item.title: ACP3 Theranostics in Prostate Cancer.
item.dc:creator: Luo Z, Chen D, Ma T, Zeng P, Li X, Shi H, Hu Z
item.description:
Authors: Luo Z, Chen D, Ma T, Zeng P, Li X, Shi H, Hu Z
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18213511
Published: 2026-Oct-31
PMID: 43026833



Abstract:
Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-targeted positron emission tomography (PET) and radioligand therapy have established a major clinical paradigm for prostate cancer theranostics. Their performance is influenced by interpatient and interlesional heterogeneity, treatment-related changes in PSMA expression, and physiological ligand uptake in organs such as the salivary glands and kidneys, creating a rationale for complementary targets with different lesion coverage and normal-tissue distribution. ACP3 (acid phosphatase 3; historical symbol ACPP) encodes prostatic acid phosphatase (PAP), which is also termed prostate-specific acid phosphatase (PSAP) in older pathology literature. PAP has served as a serum biomarker, an immunohistochemical marker of prostatic origin, and an immunotherapeutic antigen. DNA-encoded library screening identified the high-affinity PAP ligand OncoACP3, and the resulting [177Lu]Lu-OncoACP3-DOTAGA radioligand and OncoACP3-GlyPro-MMAE small-molecule drug conjugate achieved target-dependent payload delivery and antitumor activity in preclinical models. First-in-human PET and subsequent pharmacokinetic and diagnostic dosimetry studies of [68Ga]Ga-OncoACP3-DOTA demonstrated visualization of localized and metastatic prostate cancer lesions and a normal-organ distribution distinct from that of PSMA-targeted ligands. This narrative review synthesizes the molecular characteristics and biological functions of PAP, historical clinical applications, and modern ACP3-targeted imaging and therapeutic platforms. Existing studies now provide a biological foundation, preclinical proof of targeted payload delivery, and early human imaging, pharmacokinetic, and diagnostic-dosimetry evidence. Prospective development should next define the ligand-accessible PAP pool, imaging-positivity criteria, therapeutic dosimetry, and the patient groups in whom ACP3 adds value to the PSMA theranostic framework.

item.title: FIXED: A CAD/CAM Tooth-Bonded Device for Intermaxillary Fixation in Orthognathic Surgery Patients Treated With Clear Aligners.

item.description:
Authors: Sáez F, Mariscal J, Victoria C, Toledo X

Abstract:
Clear aligner therapy poses a particular challenge for orthognathic surgery: the absence of fixed orthodontic attachments compromises conventional intermaxillary fixation, which relies on brackets or skeletal anchorage. We describe FIXED, a CAD/CAM-designed, tooth-bonded intermaxillary fixation device for patients undergoing orthognathic surgery during clear aligner therapy. We illustrate the digital workflow, fabrication protocol, and surgical application in 3 patients with Class II and Class III malocclusion, one of them managed with a surgery-first protocol. In all cases, intraoperative fixation was achieved as planned, with no device-related complications during the perioperative period.

item.title: Is the Duration of Antibiotic Prophylaxis Associated With Severe Surgical Site Infection, Length of Hospital Stay, and Hospitalization Charges After Cleft Lip and/or Palate Surgery?
item.dc:creator: Nishida T, Ono S, Oshima S, Tsuda Y, Watanabe H, Matsui H, Fushimi K, Yasunaga H, Hoshi K
item.description:
Authors: Nishida T, Ono S, Oshima S, Tsuda Y, Watanabe H, Matsui H, Fushimi K, Yasunaga H, Hoshi K
