Published: 2026-Oct-30
PMID: 43039029



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite widespread antibiotic prophylaxis in cleft lip and/or palate surgery, the frequency of severe surgical site infection (SSI) requiring debridement or reoperation and the optimal duration of prophylaxis remain uncertain. Large-scale, real-world evidence is needed to better inform antibiotic prophylaxis strategies in this population. PURPOSE: To estimate the frequency of severe SSI and measure the association between antibiotic prophylaxis duration and postoperative outcomes across cleft lip and/or palate procedures. STUDY DESIGN, SETTING, SAMPLE: This nationwide, multicenter, retrospective cohort study used the Japanese Diagnosis Procedure Combination inpatient database (April 2012 to March 2022). Patients undergoing cleft lip and/or palate surgery were screened, and those with immunocompromised status, preoperative antibiotic use, or no antibiotic prophylaxis were excluded. PREDICTOR VARIABLE: Duration of postoperative antibiotic prophylaxis (short term: ≤ 2 days vs prolonged: ≥ 3 days). MAIN OUTCOME VARIABLE(S): The primary outcome was the frequency of severe SSI, defined as SSI requiring debridement or reoperation during the same hospitalization. The secondary outcomes were length of hospital stay and hospitalization charges. COVARIATES: Age, sex, body mass index, anesthesia duration, procedure category, comorbidities at admission, and teaching hospital status. ANALYSES: Multivariable regression models were used to evaluate associations between prophylaxis duration and outcomes. Subgroup analyses were performed for the 4 surgical procedure groups. The frequency of severe SSI was summarized descriptively. A P value < .05 was considered statistically significant. RESULTS: Of 17,005 patients screened, 13,333 subjects were analyzed: 6,172 (46.3%) received short-term prophylaxis, and 7,161 (53.7%) received prolonged prophylaxis. The mean (SD) age was 6.5 (9.0) years, and 7,199 (54.0%) were male. Severe SSI occurred in one subject in the prolonged group (overall frequency, 0.008%). Short-term prophylaxis was associated with a 0.5-day shorter hospital stay (95% CI: -0.8 to -0.2; P = .001) but not with hospitalization charges (adjusted mean difference, -53 US dollars [95% CI: -168 to 62]; P = .4). These findings were consistent across the 4 procedure groups. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Severe SSI requiring debridement or reoperation was extremely rare in both groups. Short-term antibiotic prophylaxis was associated with shorter hospital stays but not with hospitalization charges.

item.title: Hospital Price Transparency in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery.
item.dc:creator: Wang TT, Liang L, Peacock Z, Lee C
item.description:
Authors: Wang TT, Liang L, Peacock Z, Lee C
Journal: Journal of oral and maxillofacial surgery : official journal of the American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons | DOI: 10.1016/j.joms.2026.10.014
Published: 2026-Oct-30

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Hospital Price Transparency Rule requires hospitals to publish prices for medical and surgical services, but reporting is often incomplete. For patients paying out of pocket, discounted cash prices are particularly relevant, yet their availability for oral and maxillofacial surgery (OMS) procedures is unknown. PURPOSE: To evaluate the availability of 3 price types for common OMS procedures, including discounted cash prices, insurer-negotiated rates, and gross charges, and identify factors associated with discounted cash price availability. STUDY DESIGN, SETTING, SAMPLE: This cross-sectional study used the Turquoise Health Price Transparency Dataset. Hospitals reporting a price for at least one of 9 elective OMS procedures were included. PREDICTOR VARIABLE: The predictor was a set of factors including billing class (facility fee, professional fee), specific procedure and procedure domain (dental extraction, implant/ridge augmentation, orthognathic, temporomandibular joint, and benign pathology), and U.S. Census region. MAIN OUTCOME VARIABLE: The primary outcome was discounted cash price availability, defined as whether a discounted cash price was reported for a hospital procedure combination. Secondary outcomes were insurer-negotiated rate availability and gross charge availability. COVARIATES: None. ANALYSES: Descriptive statistics summarized availability of the 3 price types. Associations between predictors and discounted cash price availability were evaluated using χ2 tests and multivariable logistic regression. Statistical significance was set at P < .001. RESULTS: Of 7,319 hospitals, 2,717 (37.1%) reported a price for at least one selected OMS procedure. Across the 9 procedures, 95.1% of hospitals reported an insurer-negotiated rate, 21.8% a discounted cash price, and 21.0% a gross charge. When stratified by billing class, discounted cash prices were available for 7.7% of facility fees compared with 30.4% of professional fees (P < .001). In adjusted analysis, the odds that a discounted cash price was reported were lower for dental extraction (odds ratio (OR), 0.39; 95% CI, 0.24 to 0.63) and implant/ridge augmentation (OR, 0.30; 95% CI, 0.16 to 0.56) procedures compared to orthognathic procedures, and nearly 6 times greater for professional compared to facility fees (OR, 5.98; 95% CI, 4.58 to 7.81; all P < .001). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Despite widespread availability of insurer-negotiated rates, discounted cash prices were uncommon, particularly for dental services. This may limit cost information for patients paying out of pocket.

item.title: Clinical and CT body-composition model for major pathological response to neoadjuvant tislelizumab, albumin-bound paclitaxel, and nedaplatin in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.

item.description:
Authors: Xu H, Zheng W, Chen S, Wu S
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1859690
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43031628



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sarcopenia and osteoporosis are linked to poor treatment outcomes and are significantly underdiagnosed in esophageal cancer patients. Despite the promising efficacy of neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy (NACI) in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), predicting treatment response remains a major clinical hurdle. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the associations of sarcopenia and osteoporosis on pathological response and to develop a both clinical and computed tomography (CT)-based predictive model for NACI outcomes in ESCC patients. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted in 179 patients with ESCC who underwent radical resection after neoadjuvant tislelizumab, albumin-bound paclitaxel, and nedaplatin. Within each of 500 stratified bootstrap resamples, five-fold cross-validation was used to determine the optimal LASSO penalty parameter, followed by Firth logistic regression. Aggregated out-of-bag predictions underwent five-fold cross-fitted recalibration. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were evaluated using the AUC, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, Brier score, calibration intercept and slope, Hosmer-Lemeshow test, and decision curve analysis. RESULTS: Major pathological response (MPR) rates were 70.0%, 40.0%, 22.0%, and 8.3% in the control, osteoporosis-only, sarcopenia-only, and osteosarcopenia groups, respectively. In multivariable Firth logistic regression, lower tumor grading, absence of comorbidities, absence of lymphovascular invasion, absence of sarcopenia, and a higher intermuscular adipose tissue (IMAT) area percentage were associated with a greater likelihood of achieving MPR, whereas osteoporosis was not associated with MPR (P = 0.130). The cross-fitted recalibrated model achieved an AUC of 0.885 (95% CI, 0.835-0.934), with 0.818 accuracy, 0.840 sensitivity, and 0.800 specificity at a threshold of 0.405. Calibration was satisfactory (Brier score, 0.136; intercept, -0.009; slope, 0.960; Hosmer-Lemeshow P = 0.219), and decision curve analysis showed clinical net benefit across thresholds of 0.08-0.80. CONCLUSION: Absence of sarcopenia and a higher IMAT area percentage were associated with a greater likelihood of achieving major pathological response. The combined clinical and CT-based model showed good internally validated performance.

item.title: Sequencing-informed, patient-specific droplet digital PCR assays for circulating tumor DNA monitoring in recurrent or metastatic head and neck cancer: a pilot study.
item.dc:creator: Amodio LL, Grossmann L, Gächter S, Nowak M, Schaufelberger M, Mennicke C, Rahmani-Khajouei S, Zoche M, Moch H, Weber A, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Amodio LL, Grossmann L, Gächter S, Nowak M, Schaufelberger M, Mennicke C, Rahmani-Khajouei S, Zoche M, Moch H, Weber A, et al.
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1984504
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43031620



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (R/M HNSCC), early identification of treatment response remains challenging because imaging may be delayed or confounded by treatment-related changes and atypical response patterns under immunotherapy. Serial circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) analysis may provide a minimally invasive measure of tumor dynamics and complement conventional imaging. We therefore investigated the feasibility and clinical relevance of patient-specific droplet digital PCR (ddPCR)-based ctDNA monitoring. METHODS: Nine patients with R/M HNSCC underwent tumor genomic profiling using FoundationOne® CDx as part of routine clinical care. Patient-specific single-nucleotide variants, including pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants and technically suitable variants of uncertain significance, were selected for ddPCR assay development. Plasma samples were collected before and/or during systemic treatment, and ctDNA kinetics were assessed in relation to radiologic response, progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS). RESULTS: Sixteen single-target ddPCR assays were successfully established and combined into ten patient-specific single- or multi-target assay configurations. A total of 21 plasma samples were analyzed, and technically valid measurements were obtained for all samples. Pretreatment plasma was available for seven patients, of whom three (42.9%) had detectable ctDNA. Across all time points, ctDNA was detected at least once in six of nine patients (66.7%). Among the six patients with serial sampling, ctDNA kinetics showed descriptive agreement with radiologic assessment in five (83.3%). The single patient with increasing ctDNA developed progressive disease, whereas decreasing or stable ctDNA was accompanied by partial response or stable disease in four patients; one patient showed a mixed radiologic response. In an exploratory descriptive comparison, the single patient with increasing ctDNA had shorter observed PFS and OS than the five patients with decreasing or stable ctDNA levels. Given the group size of one patient, this observation is hypothesis-generating and does not establish a prognostic association. CONCLUSIONS: Patient-specific ddPCR-based ctDNA monitoring was technically feasible and showed agreement with radiologic assessment in most evaluable patients. These proof-of-concept findings support prospective evaluation of patient-specific ddPCR as a focused approach for longitudinal monitoring in R/M HNSCC; its comparative clinical utility and cost-effectiveness remain to be established.

item.title: A pretreatment TNM-metabolic vulnerability score with EBV DNA adjustment for risk stratification in non-metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Zhong J, Zhou C, Yi Q, Zhong K, Chen Z, Ouyang X, Xu C, Liao J, Chen W, Zhang X
item.description:
Authors: Zhong J, Zhou C, Yi Q, Zhong K, Chen Z, Ouyang X, Xu C, Liao J, Chen W, Zhang X
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1914286

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: TNM stage and pretreatment plasma Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) DNA are central to risk assessment in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), but they do not fully capture host metabolic reserve. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 160 patients with non-metastatic NPC treated from 2013 to 2022. The integrated metabolic vulnerability score (IMVS; range, 0-3) assigned 1 point each for stage IVA, triglyceride-to-HDL cholesterol ratio <1.217, and body mass index <23.79 kg/m2. Cox regression and bootstrap internal validation evaluated progression-free survival (PFS), with EBV DNA included as an adjustment variable. A broader 271-patient cohort from the same institution was used only for internal sensitivity analysis. RESULTS: Thirty-three PFS events occurred in the modeling cohort. Five-year PFS was 100.0%, 91.9%, 72.1%, and 50.0% for IMVS scores 0, 1, 2, and 3, respectively. IMVS remained associated with PFS after adjustment for EBV DNA status (HR, 2.74; bootstrap percentile 95% CI, 1.89-4.75; P<0.001), although EBV DNA status itself was not independently significant in this cohort. The optimism-corrected AUC was 0.715 for stage IVA, THR, and BMI and 0.727 after adding EBV DNA. In the broader same-institution cohort, the association persisted but was attenuated (HR, 1.55; 95% CI, 1.14-2.10; P = 0.005). CONCLUSION: IMVS is an exploratory, low-cost risk-stratification tool that may complement, rather than replace, TNM stage and plasma EBV DNA. Prospective external validation and recalibration of the data-derived thresholds are required before clinical use.

item.title: Synchronous Differentiated Thyroid Carcinoma in Non-Invasive Follicular Thyroid Neoplasm with Papillary-like Nuclear Features (NIFTP): Prevalence, Pathological Profile, and Limits of Pre-Operative Risk Prediction in a Multicentre Cohort.
item.dc:creator: Dobrinja C, Mastronardi M, Bernardi S, Bonati E, Bononi M, Calò PG, Canu GL, Cappellacci F, Chiofalo MG, Pasquale L, et al.
item.description:

Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18213505
Published: 2026-Oct-30
PMID: 43026826



Abstract:
Background/Objectives: Non-invasive follicular thyroid neoplasm with papillary-like nuclear features (NIFTP) was reclassified as a non-malignant entity in 2016 to reduce overtreatment. A proportion of NIFTP-containing glands nonetheless harbour a synchronous differentiated thyroid carcinoma (DTC). We quantified its prevalence and pathological profile and assessed whether routinely collected pre-operative variables identify affected patients. Methods: A multicentre retrospective cohort of 1185 adults with NIFTP confirmed at second histological review, operated on between 2017 and 2023 in 22 centres. The outcome was a synchronous DTC in the surgical specimen. A weighted random forest and an elastic-net logistic regression based on 13 pre-operative predictors were evaluated with 20-times repeated five-fold cross-validation, with all data-driven steps nested within training folds, and with leave-one-centre-out and temporal validation. Results: A synchronous DTC was present in 61 patients (5.1%; 95% CI 4.0-6.6; 6.2% after review of the stored reports), with marked between-centre variation (none recorded in eight centres). Fifty-eight carcinomas (95%) were pT1a; none had gross extra-thyroidal extension or nodal metastasis (nodes examined in 27 patients), and none met the 2025 American Thyroid Association criteria mandating a more extensive operation. No pre-operative variable differed between groups after multiplicity adjustment. The cross-validated AUROC was 0.56 (95% CI 0.47-0.65) for the random forest and 0.58 (0.48-0.67) for the elastic net; the within-centre concordance was 0.48 and the temporal-validation AUROC 0.39, and decision-curve analysis showed no net benefit over default strategies. Conclusions: About one in twenty NIFTP-containing specimens harbours a synchronous DTC, usually a low-risk papillary microcarcinoma. Routinely available pre-operative variables do not identify these patients; management should be guided by the pathology of the carcinoma itself.

item.title: Tumour Cell-Associated Heterogeneity in Antiviral Immunity Shapes Influenza Responses and Immune-Modulatory Signalling in Lung Cancer.
item.dc:creator: Miles MA, Rosano I, Liong S, Logan JM, O'Leary JJ, Brooks DA, Selemidis S
item.description:
Authors: Miles MA, Rosano I, Liong S, Logan JM, O'Leary JJ, Brooks DA, Selemidis S
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18213502
Published: 2026-Oct-30
PMID: 43026823



Abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Respiratory viral infections occur within the same anatomical niche as lung cancer, yet how lung cancer cells respond to infection and how these responses influence antiviral and inflammatory signalling remain poorly understood. This study investigated innate immune responses to influenza A virus (IAV) infection across a panel of lung epithelial cell lines. METHODS: Non-malignant bronchial epithelial and non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) cell lines representing adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma were infected with IAV. Antiviral and inflammatory gene expression, viral RNA and protein detection, infection-induced cell death, pattern recognition receptor expression, and immune checkpoint ligand expression were assessed using molecular, biochemical and flow cytometric approaches. Interferon (IFN) receptor blockade and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species scavenging were used to investigate selected signalling mechanisms. RESULTS: NSCLC cell lines exhibited heterogeneous innate immune responses to IAV infection, with differential regulation of RNA-sensing pathways and canonical antiviral signalling components. Although IFN responses were retained, NSCLC cells exhibited reduced infection-induced apoptosis and prolonged viral RNA and protein detection compared with non-malignant epithelial cells. IAV infection was also associated with changes in DNA-sensing receptor expression, including TLR9, and increased expression of the immune checkpoint ligand PD-L1. CONCLUSIONS: These findings identify substantial cell line-associated heterogeneity in antiviral responses to IAV across lung epithelial cell lines, including NSCLC cells. The observed differences in viral RNA and protein detection, cell death responses and immune-modulatory signalling provide a framework for understanding how respiratory viral infections may interact with lung cancer cells to shape antiviral and inflammatory responses within the tumour environment.

item.title: Real-World Activity and Safety of Metronomic Cyclophosphamide in Advanced Soft-Tissue Sarcoma: The Multicenter MeRCY Study.
item.dc:creator: Bolognini C, Falcoz A, Simon P, Calcagno F, Hervieu A, Isambert N, Desmoulins I, Causeret S, Thibouw D, Kalbacher E, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Bolognini C, Falcoz A, Simon P, Calcagno F, Hervieu A, Isambert N, Desmoulins I, Causeret S, Thibouw D, Kalbacher E, et al.
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18213497
Published: 2026-Oct-30
PMID: 43026818



Abstract:
Background/Objectives: Metronomic cyclophosphamide (MCP) is sometimes used for advanced soft-tissue sarcoma (STS) when standard therapies are unsuitable. We assessed its activity and safety in routine practice. Methods: This French three-center retrospective study included 60 adults with unresectable or metastatic STS who started MCP in 2008-2021. Patients received oral cyclophosphamide 50 mg twice daily on days 1-7 of 14-day cycles; 12 (20%) also received prednisolone during treatment weeks. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS). Results: Median age was 70 years; 55% had ECOG performance status 2-3. Median PFS and overall survival (OS) were 2.6 months (95% CI, 1.8-3.6) and 6.4 months (95% CI, 4.2-9.3), respectively. The objective response rate was 5.0% (3/60; exact 95% CI, 1.0-13.9%) and the disease control rate was 21.7% (13/60; exact 95% CI, 12.1-34.2%); ten patients (16.7%) were not radiologically evaluable. In 21 patients aged >65 years treated in the first- or second-line setting, median PFS and OS were 3.2 and 7.7 months. Treatment-related adverse events were documented in 16 patients (26.7%), with no grade ≥3 events recorded. Conclusions: Intermittent low-dose MCP showed limited antitumor activity but favorable clinician-documented short-term tolerability in this multicenter cohort. Alongside prospective evidence, the results do not support routine use in unselected patients. MCP may retain an individualized palliative role when established systemic therapy is unsuitable.

item.title: Temporal Patterns of Patient-Reported Symptoms, Jaw Function, Oral Parafunctions, and Psychological Outcomes After Orthognathic Surgery in Skeletal Class III Patients.
item.dc:creator: Adeviye Çankaya RT, Bor A, Tunç O, Akbulut N
item.description:
Authors: Adeviye Çankaya RT, Bor A, Tunç O, Akbulut N
Journal: Journal of oral and maxillofacial surgery : official journal of the American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons | DOI: 10.1016/j.joms.2026.10.009
Published: 2026-Oct-29
PMID: 43039030



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dentofacial deformities can affect jaw function, oral health-related quality of life, and psychological well-being. Longitudinal evidence assessing multiple patient-reported outcomes remains limited. PURPOSE: To measure temporal changes in 6 patient-reported outcomes following bimaxillary orthognathic surgery. STUDY DESIGN, SETTING, AND SAMPLE: This prospective longitudinal cohort study included consecutive adults with skeletal Class III dentofacial deformity who underwent bimaxillary surgery at Ondokuz Mayıs University between October 2024 and June 2025 and were followed for 6 months postoperatively. Patients with skeletal Class I or II deformity, clinically significant facial asymmetry requiring additional procedures, revision surgery, or American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status II or higher were excluded. PREDICTOR VARIABLE: The predictor was assessment time: 1 week preoperatively (T0), and 6 weeks (T1), 3 months (T2), and 6 months (T3) postoperatively. OUTCOME VARIABLES: Outcomes were Fonseca Anamnestic Index (FAI), 8-item Jaw Functional Limitation Scale (JFLS-8), Oral Behaviors Checklist (OBC), 14-item Oral Health Impact Profile (OHIP-14), 7-item Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD-7) scale, and 9-item Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9) scores. Lower scores indicate less symptom burden (FAI), functional limitation (JFLS-8), oral behavior frequency (OBC), adverse oral health impact (OHIP-14), anxiety symptom severity (GAD-7), or depressive symptom severity (PHQ-9). No single primary outcome was prespecified. COVARIATES: Age and sex. ANALYSES: Friedman tests and Bonferroni-corrected Wilcoxon signed-rank tests (P < .0083) evaluated temporal changes. Secondary generalized estimating equation models adjusted for age and sex. RESULTS: All 37 participants completed follow-up (mean age, 20.9 ± 2.3 years; 26 female [70.3%]). Median baseline and 6-month scores, respectively, were FAI, 45 and 15; JFLS-8, 15 and 5; OBC, 25 and 18; OHIP-14, 20 and 10; PHQ-9, 7 and 5; and GAD-7, 5 and 4. Overall time effects were statistically significant for all outcomes (P < .001, except PHQ-9, P = .030). Baseline-to-6-month comparisons met the corrected threshold for FAI, JFLS-8, OBC, and OHIP-14, but not PHQ-9 or GAD-7. CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: Patient-reported symptom burden, jaw functional limitation, oral behaviors, and adverse oral health impacts were lower at 6 months than at baseline, whereas psychological changes were less consistent. These temporal associations do not establish causal effects of surgery.

item.title: Immunosenescence and Inflammaging in the Pathogenesis of Non-Melanoma Skin Cancer.
item.dc:creator: Mihalj M, Mioč NF, Sabljić I, Čeprnja ZŠ, Tokić S, Buljan M
item.description:
Authors: Mihalj M, Mioč NF, Sabljić I, Čeprnja ZŠ, Tokić S, Buljan M
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18213481
Published: 2026-Oct-28
PMID: 43026802



Abstract:
Non-melanoma skin cancer (NMSC) is the most frequently diagnosed malignancy worldwide, and its incidence rises disproportionately with age. While cumulative ultraviolet (UV) exposure is the dominant recognised risk factor, it does not fully account for the steep age-associated increase in NMSC, suggesting that additional, underrecognised mechanisms operate in older skin. This review synthesises evidence that immune senescence (the age-related remodelling of innate and adaptive immunity) is a central and partly modifiable driver of NMSC aetiopathogenesis. We first outline the classical risk factors and the epidemiological and economic burden of NMSC, and revisit the proposal to regard recurrent NMSC as a chronic disease. We then examine four interlocking, age-associated processes: the accumulation of senescent cells and their pro-inflammatory secretory phenotype ("inflammaging") in the skin microenvironment; UV-induced suppression of cutaneous immune function; age-related dysbiosis of the skin microbiome and its impact on antitumour immunity; and the systemic decline of T-cell-mediated tumour immunosurveillance. We integrate these processes into a framework in which immune senescence contributes to the progression of accumulated cutaneous damage to overt malignancy, and consider the implications for prevention (including senotherapeutics, microbiome modulation, and immune-stratified surveillance) that extend beyond UV-directed measures alone.

item.title: A Literature-Derived Muscle Wasting-Related Prognostic Signature Identifies ZBTB7C as a Candidate Associated with Tumor-Related Skeletal Muscle Alterations in Esophageal Cancer.
item.dc:creator: Li Y, Xie C, Chen R, Ming Z, Huang H, Ding S
item.description:
Authors: Li Y, Xie C, Chen R, Ming Z, Huang H, Ding S
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18213479
Published: 2026-Oct-28
PMID: 43026800



Abstract:
Background: Skeletal muscle wasting is a frequent systemic complication of esophageal cancer and is associated with unfavorable clinical outcomes. However, the relationships among tumor-associated molecular characteristics, patient prognosis, and skeletal muscle alterations remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify prognostically relevant genes from a literature-curated muscle wasting-related gene set and investigate the potential association of ZBTB7C with tumor-related skeletal muscle alterations in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). Methods: Transcriptomic and survival data from the complete TCGA-ESCA cohort and the independent GSE53625 cohort were analyzed using a predefined set of genes implicated in muscle wasting-related biology. Differential expression analysis, consensus clustering, Cox regression, LASSO-Cox analysis, survival analysis, functional enrichment, and immune-related analyses were performed. A six-gene prognostic signature was constructed in the TCGA cohort and externally evaluated in GSE53625. ZBTB7C was subsequently investigated using human ESCC tissues and cell lines, Zbtb7c-overexpressing AKR cells, AKR-conditioned medium-treated C2C12 myotubes, and an immunocompetent AKR/C57BL/6 syngeneic tumor model. Results: A total of 32 literature-curated muscle wasting-related genes were retained for analysis. A six-gene prognostic signature comprising ZBTB7C, DDIT3, RNF157, AMOTL1, TTLL12, and PDLIM2 was associated with overall survival, although its discriminatory performance was limited in the external validation cohort. ZBTB7C expression was reduced in ESCC tissues and cell lines, and higher expression was associated with favorable survival. Zbtb7c overexpression reduced PCNA expression in AKR tumor cells. Conditioned medium from Zbtb7c-overexpressing AKR cells attenuated MuRF-1 and Atrogin-1 expression, partially restored AKT, FOXO3A, and P70S6K phosphorylation, and increased global protein synthesis in C2C12 myotubes. In vivo, Zbtb7c overexpression suppressed tumor growth and was accompanied by preservation of gastrocnemius muscle mass, attenuation of muscle protein homeostasis-related alterations, and a smaller decline in all-limb grip strength. Conclusions: These findings identify ZBTB7C as an exploratory candidate associated with esophageal cancer prognosis and tumor-related skeletal muscle alterations. However, its muscle-related effects cannot be fully distinguished from reduced tumor burden, and further mechanistic and clinical validation is required before its potential utility as a biomarker or therapeutic target can be established.

item.title: Factors Associated with Level II and V Involvement in Lateral Neck Dissection for pN1b Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Díaz Ríos P, Bustos Merlo AB, Arcelus Martínez JI, Becerra Massare A, Muñoz Pérez NV, Villar Del Moral JM
item.description:
Authors: Díaz Ríos P, Bustos Merlo AB, Arcelus Martínez JI, Becerra Massare A, Muñoz Pérez NV, Villar Del Moral JM
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18213473
Published: 2026-Oct-28
PMID: 43026794



Abstract:
Background: Lateral neck dissection is the standard surgical treatment for patients with papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) and lateral cervical lymph node metastases (pN1b). However, the optimal extent of dissection remains debated, particularly for levels II and V. We examined patterns of nodal involvement and factors associated with metastases at these levels. Methods: This single-center retrospective study included 70 patients with pN1b PTC who underwent lateral neck dissection between 2019 and 2025. Demographic, clinical, surgical, and pathological variables were analyzed. The lymph node ratio (LNR), defined as metastatic nodes divided by harvested nodes, was dichotomized at the cohort median. Bivariate associations were assessed using Pearson's χ2 test, Fisher's exact test, or the Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact test, as appropriate; p < 0.05 indicated statistical significance. Results: Median age was 46 years and 60% were female. Involvement was highest at levels III (82.9%) and IV (65.7%), followed by II (55.7%) and V (23.9%). Median LNR was 0.25. Level II involvement was more frequent in male patients (71.4% vs. 45.2%; p = 0.031) and patients with high versus low LNR (76.5% vs. 36.1%; p = 0.001). Histological subtype was associated with level V involvement (p = 0.027), predominantly in classic PTC. Conclusions: Male sex and higher LNR were associated with level II involvement in bivariate analyses; an exploratory association was also observed between histological subtype and level V involvement. These findings do not establish independent predictors or justify altering the extent of neck dissection. Larger cohorts and multivariable analyses should validate these findings.

item.title: Clinical influence of interproximal wedge positions with a modified image receptor-holding device for bitewing radiography.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the influence of different positions of the interproximal wedge of a modified image receptor-holding device (IRHD) on proximal surfaces overlapping in intraoral bitewing radiography. Patients were randomly assigned to the IRHD and interproximal wedge direction on each side of the arch. Images were obtained using a digital radiographic system. Two oral radiologists independently evaluated proximal surface overlap. The overlap rate was expressed as absolute and relative frequencies and compared using the chi-square test with a significance level of 5%. Operator perception and patient comfort were descriptively evaluated using questionnaires. RESULTS: Statistically significant differences were observed among IRHDs (P < .05). item.title: DAMPs and NETs in Thyroid Diseases: Biological, Diagnostic, and Translational Perspectives.
item.dc:creator: Waczyński K, Choromańska B, Maciejczyk M, Lewoc-Magnuszewska M, Tkaczuk A, Grymuza J, Dadan J, Myśliwiec P
item.description:
Authors: Waczyński K, Choromańska B, Maciejczyk M, Lewoc-Magnuszewska M, Tkaczuk A, Grymuza J, Dadan J, Myśliwiec P
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18213469
Published: 2026-Oct-27
PMID: 43026790



Abstract:
Thyroid diseases encompass a broad spectrum of autoimmune, inflammatory, and neoplastic disorders, yet current diagnostic approaches provide limited insight into innate immune activation and tumor-associated inflammatory remodeling. Damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) and neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) have emerged as interconnected mediators of sterile inflammation with potential relevance to thyroid carcinogenesis, disease progression, and biomarker development. This narrative review synthesized literature identified through PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus to evaluate the biological, diagnostic, and translational significance of DAMP- and NET-associated pathways in thyroid diseases, with particular emphasis on thyroid cancer. DAMPs such as high-mobility group box 1 (HMGB1), S100A8/A9, serum amyloid A, heat shock proteins, and extracellular nucleic acids may sustain inflammatory signaling through pattern-recognition receptors and contribute to tumor proliferation, angiogenesis, immune modulation, and therapeutic resistance. In parallel, circulating analytes associated with NET biology-including nonspecific cell-free DNA (cfDNA) and nucleosomes, pathway-associated citrullinated histone H3 (CitH3), and composite myeloperoxidase-DNA (MPO-DNA) complexes-have shown associations with thyroid malignancy, dedifferentiated disease, metastatic presentation, and greater disease severity. Experimental data further suggest that aggressive thyroid cancer cells, particularly anaplastic thyroid carcinoma, can induce extracellular trap formation and exploit neutrophil-derived signals to support tumor growth. However, limited disease specificity, assay heterogeneity, and the predominance of small or exploratory cohorts currently restrict clinical implementation. Future strategies should prioritize standardized, prospective validation of multimarker panels integrating DAMP- and NET-related analytes with imaging, cytology, molecular diagnostics, and clinicopathological risk stratification to determine whether they provide incremental value for diagnosis, prognostication, and longitudinal monitoring in thyroid cancer.

item.title: Temporal Associations Between Thyroid Cancer Epidemiological Trends and Classification Revisions.
item.dc:creator: Trovato M, Pandiyan B, Ferrari SM, Famà F, Benvenga S
item.description:

Abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated potential temporal associations between international histopathological classifications, staging updates, and the long-term divergence observed between papillary thyroid cancer (PTC) and follicular thyroid cancer (FTC) incidence trends. Applying an advanced statistical protocol comprising the recursive Supremum Chow Test, Piecewise Segmented Regression with Regime Switching (PSR-RS), and a non-linear Markov-Switching Intercept and Slope (MSIA) model, we analyzed population-level annual incidence rates (AIR) in the United States from 1975 to 2023. METHODS: We implemented a two-pronged approach to identify and validate structural trend changes in incidence trends. Approach 1 tracked endogenous, data-driven incidence shifts, while Approach 2 tested the fixed calendar milestones corresponding to the official publication dates of major classifications. Crucially, this multistage analytical protocol was applied directly to the individual PTC and FTC series, as well as to the scale-independent log ratio, ln(PTC/FTC) and aggregate diagnostic gap timelines. RESULTS: The results show that the incidence gap between the two cancers widened until 2014 and stabilized thereafter. AG quadrupled from 2.9 per 100,000 population in 1975 (PTC AIR = 3.6 minus FTC AIR = 0.7) to 11.6 in 2014 (PTC AIR = 12.8 minus FTC AIR = 1.2) with no further increase thereafter (AG = 11.6 in 2022 and 2023). Under Approach 1, the natural breakpoints partitioned the timelines into highly diverse behavioral segments. Specifically, the data identified five evolutionary regimes for PTC, three independent regimes for FTC, and four distinct regimes for AG. The breakpoint identified in 1987 coincided with the staging updates introduced that year and marked a clear change in the incidence trends of both histotypes. Between 1987 and 1991, PTC incidence increased, while FTC incidence declined toward its historical minimum. Despite these changes, the aggregate diagnostic gap continued along its existing trend, with no structural break detected. The 2004 WHO third edition corresponded to a systematic upward level shift (β2 = +4.1500) associated with the formal codification of microcarcinomas. Finally, both analytical approaches converged on 2014 as a significant historical turning point in the slowing of incidence growth. This phase is characterized by a significant negative slope change (Δβ = -0.35) consistent with conservative classification updates and subsequent stabilization at a structural plateau. CONCLUSIONS: The progressively widening AIR gap between PTC and FTC does not appear to reflect a purely biological phenomenon. Instead, these population-level changes are highly consistent with systematic reporting shifts and diagnostic thresholds introduced in successive international staging and histopathological classifications.

item.title: Rab23 Drives Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma Invasion via ERK-Mediated Autophagy Activation.
item.dc:creator: Wu J, Feng Z, Xie C, Yang J
item.description:
Authors: Wu J, Feng Z, Xie C, Yang J
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18213458
Published: 2026-Oct-26
PMID: 43026780



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) is the second most prevalent non-melanoma skin cancer worldwide, with increasing incidence and considerable mortality following metastasis. Ras-associated binding protein 23 (Rab23) has been implicated in cSCC progression, but its molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. METHODS: Rab23, Beclin1, and LC3-II protein expression was compared across human cSCC, actinic keratosis, and normal skin tissues. Rab23-dependent changes in autophagy-related markers, autophagic vacuoles, migration, invasion, and wound healing were investigated in oral SCC-derived Sa3 cells and cSCC models A431 and HSC-5. GTP dependence, responses to rapamycin and chloroquine, and AKT/mTOR and MEK/ERK1/2 signaling were assessed, including MEK1/2 inhibition with U0126. Public transcriptomic and spatial transcriptomic datasets were also analyzed. RESULTS: Rab23 protein expression was significantly elevated in cSCC lesions compared with normal skin and actinic keratosis, accompanied by increased Beclin1 and LC3-II levels, and correlated positively with both markers. Rab23 overexpression increased Beclin1 and LC3-II expression and decreased p62 in a GTP-dependent manner. It also enhanced autophagic vacuole formation, migration, invasion, and wound healing. Rapamycin potentiated these effects, whereas chloroquine abrogated them. Rab23 activated both AKT/mTOR and MEK/ERK1/2 signaling; however, U0126 abolished Rab23-induced autophagy marker upregulation and migratory capacity. Transcriptomic and spatial transcriptomic analyses further supported the clinical relevance of the Rab23-ERK-autophagy axis in SCC aggressiveness. CONCLUSIONS: Rab23 promotes cSCC invasion, at least in part, through ERK-dependent autophagy enhancement, highlighting this signaling axis as a potential therapeutic target for cSCC.

item.title: Oral Cavity Cancer and the Subsequent Incidence of Other Cancer Diagnoses: A Retrospective Cohort Study in German General Practices.
item.dc:creator: Cirkel LL, Wöstmann B, Kostev K
item.description:
Authors: Cirkel LL, Wöstmann B, Kostev K
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18213444
Published: 2026-Oct-24
PMID: 43026766



Abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Subsequent cancer diagnoses are well documented after oral cavity cancer, particularly within the upper aerodigestive tract. However, evidence from routine primary care is limited, although such data may provide complementary insights into the long-term documentation of subsequent cancer diagnoses. This study examined subsequent cancer diagnoses after oral cavity cancer in German general practices and assessed the influence of anatomically adjacent cancer codes. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used the IQVIA Disease Analyzer database. Adults with a first documented oral cavity cancer (International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision [ICD-10]: C02-C06) recorded in German general practices between 2005 and 2024, with at least 12 months of prior observation and no earlier cancer, were included. A landmark design was applied to both cohorts: follow-up began 365 days after the index date, and individuals not observed beyond that date or with a cancer documented in the first year were excluded. Patients were matched 1:10 on age, sex, index year, consultation frequency in the 12 months before the index date and Charlson Comorbidity Index. The outcome definition was identical in both cohorts (ICD-10 C00-C97, excluding C02-C06 and C77-C80). Cox regression with robust variance estimation was used. RESULTS: A total of 1043 patients with oral cavity cancer and 10,430 matched individuals were analyzed. A cancer diagnosis was documented in 16.8% and 6.9% of individuals, respectively, corresponding to 38.0 and 15.6 per 1000 person-years (hazard ratio [HR] 2.43; 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.06-2.87). The HR was highest among patients aged ≤60 years (HR 4.07) and lowest among those aged >70 years (HR 1.48; p for interaction <0.001). Subsequent diagnoses involving the upper aerodigestive and respiratory tracts were disproportionately represented in the oral cavity cancer cohort. Excluding anatomically adjacent cancer codes attenuated the association (HR 1.81; 95% CI 1.51-2.17). CONCLUSIONS: Oral cavity cancer was associated with a higher incidence of subsequently documented cancer diagnoses. The association was attenuated but persisted after excluding anatomically adjacent and potentially ambiguous cancer codes; the data do not establish whether these diagnoses represent confirmed second primary malignancies.

item.title: Endoscopic Transorbital Approach to Skull Base Lesions: Implications, Limitations, and Future Perspectives.
item.dc:creator: Rawson C, Ofori-Ntiamoah G, Karsy M, Pahlevani M
item.description:
Authors: Rawson C, Ofori-Ntiamoah G, Karsy M, Pahlevani M
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18213443
Published: 2026-Oct-24
PMID: 43026765



Abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: The endoscopic transorbital approach (ETOA) has emerged over little more than a decade as a minimally invasive corridor to the anterior and middle cranial fossae, reaching territory lateral to the optic nerve and internal carotid artery that is difficult to access endonasally. Its flagship indication is the spheno-orbital meningioma, where the corridor aligns with the pathology and functions best as a planned, often decompressive strategy rather than a route to radical resection. This narrative review synthesizes the current evidence and defines the approach's role, limitations, and priorities. METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for English-language anatomical studies, clinical series, systematic reviews, and meta-analyses on the transorbital approach published between January 2016 and August 2026. RESULTS: The evidence remains dominated by small, retrospective, single-center series and a handful of recent meta-analyses. Reported short-term outcomes-favorable proptosis relief, acceptable visual and cranial-nerve results, low pooled complication rates, and short recovery-are encouraging but constrained by short follow-up, heterogeneous nomenclature, and outcome reporting that grades residual tumor globally rather than by anatomical compartment. Gross total resection rates are lower than after transcranial surgery, and oncological equivalence has not been established. Technical, reconstructive, ophthalmic, and anatomical factors define the corridor's ceiling, and ETOA is best positioned against endonasal and transcranial alternatives as a complementary rather than competing tool. CONCLUSIONS: ETOA is an established corridor whose maturation depends on reconstructive refinement, a flatter learning curve, standardized terminology and outcome sets, and prospective comparative data-consolidation rather than anatomical expansion.
